title: Account Executive Nordics
description:
Who is Litmus 

Litmus is building the data foundation that powers industrial AI.

AI doesn’t work without real-world, contextualized data - Litmus makes that data usable. As AI adoption accelerates, most industrial environments still can’t access or use their operational data. We solve that gap.

We’re a growth-stage software company helping manufacturers access, structure, and use real-time data from machines, systems, and sensors at the edge. Our platform sits at the intersection of edge computing, AI, and industrial operations, enabling some of the world’s largest companies to run operations in real time, reduce downtime, and optimize production.

Backed by leading investors and trusted by global manufacturers and partners like Google, Microsoft, Dell, Oracle, and Mitsubishi, Litmus is powering the shift toward software-defined manufacturing.

Why join Litmus 

Build the infrastructure that makes industrial AI possible 

AI is moving beyond the cloud and into the physical world. At Litmus, you’ll build the infrastructure that enables real-time data to power AI and machine learning systems in production environments.

Work on problems where software meets the real world 

Most AI systems fail without access to real-world data. You’ll build the layer that makes them viable in production. We solve challenges at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time data, and industrial constraints — where reliability, scale, and performance are non-negotiable.

Have real impact, fast 

You’ll work on systems used by real customers in production, with direct impact on product and company trajectory. As a scaling company, we move quickly. You’ll have ownership, visibility, and the ability to shape both product and company as we scale.

Join a high-performance team 

We’re building a team that holds a high bar and pushes each other to improve. You’ll work alongside experienced operators, engineers, and leaders who have done this before and are building again at scale. We hire people who take ownership, move quickly, and care about outcomes. No passengers.

Our culture 

At Litmus, the team is collaborative, curious, and low ego. People are scrappy, take ownership, and look for ways to make an impact. We value empathy just as much as execution, whether that’s in how we build, how we communicate, or how we support each other.

We’re a growing company, so things move quickly and not everything is perfectly defined. If you enjoy figuring things out, working closely with others, and making steady progress, you’ll do well here.

About the role

Litmus is hiring an Account Executive to own and grow new business with industrial manufacturers across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland and Finland.

Litmus is an industrial DataOps and edge AI platform. We help manufacturers connect, normalize and use data from their plants, from shop-floor assets up to the cloud. Our customers use Litmus to break down OT data silos and scale analytics and AI across sites.

You will be the face of Litmus in the Nordics. You will build pipeline, run complex enterprise sales cycles end to end, and work closely with our pre-sales team, hyperscaler partners (Microsoft, AWS, Google, Databricks) and system integrators. You will report in to the VP EMEA.

What you will do

• Own a Nordic territory and its revenue target, from prospecting to signed contract and expansion.

• Build and qualify pipeline through outbound, events, partners and inbound leads.

• Run discovery with plant, operations, OT and IT stakeholders up to C-level, and map their business case for change.

• Lead structured, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles, including proofs of value, commercial proposals and negotiation.

• Work hand in hand with pre-sales on demos, solution design and technical validation.

• Co-sell with hyperscalers and system integrators, and develop partner-sourced opportunities in your region.

• Keep forecasts and opportunity data accurate in Salesforce.

• Expand existing accounts from first site to multi-site and global rollouts.

• Bring market feedback back to product, marketing and leadership.

What you bring

Segment experience (required) 

• 5+ years of B2B enterprise software sales, with a proven record of meeting or beating quota.

• Direct sales experience in industrial software: IIoT, industrial DataOps, data historians, MES, SCADA, edge computing or manufacturing analytics.

• A solid grasp of the OT/IT landscape in manufacturing, and of how plant data flows from machines to the cloud.

• Experience selling into manufacturing, process industries, energy or similar industrial sectors.

Nordic market knowledge (required) 

• An established network among industrial manufacturers in the Nordics.

• A working understanding of Nordic buying culture, decision-making and procurement.

• Familiarity with the regional partner and system integrator landscape.

• Fluency in English and at least one Nordic language (Swedish, Norwegian, Danish or Finnish).

How you work 

• Comfortable running long, complex deals with many stakeholders.

• Disciplined in qualification and forecasting (MEDDIC/MEDDPICC or similar).

• Self-driven and at ease building a territory in a growing team.

Nice to have

• Experience selling alongside Microsoft, AWS, Google or Databricks.

• Track record of displacing incumbent industrial software, such as historians or legacy integration tools.

• Experience in an early-stage or scale-up team in a new region.

Travel and location

• Up to 40% travel within the Nordics and to EMEA team and partner events.

• Based in the Nordics, ideally near Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen or Helsinki.

title: Software Engineer II, System Integration

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary 

At Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies we have the exciting challenge of building and integrating a core technology platform into multiple brands across many different regions. Critical to the success of this endeavor are the software integration engineers who serve as our critical interface and system advocate with domain teams across the vehicle. As a software integration engineer you will be the go-to person for system understanding, issue triage, system development, and escalation and as a result have opportunities to work across the entire vehicle system.

This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite, with occasional travel to other company and partner sites as needed.

Responsibilities 

- Directly support bring up of new platforms and software integration from the prototype stage all the way through production

- Drive development, integration and delivery of new system features, filling in wherever necessary technically to achieve system goals

- Drive necessary test automation and fleet monitoring tools to ensure persistent quality of vehicle features

- Collaborate cross-functionally with feature partners and domain teams to improve system design, test coverage, and resolve issues

- Perform fleet-level analysis of system performance to drive development and integration priorities

- Travel as necessary to work with domain counterparts and grow your own understanding of vehicle systems and tools.

Qualifications 

Minimum Qualifications: 

- Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field

- Experience developing in Python (preferred), Rust (preferred), C, C++,, Golang, or

- Experience with systems engineering and analysis

- Experience working on complex, cross-functional, distributed embedded systems

- Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills

Preferred Qualifications 

- Experience working in a continuous integration environment

- Experience with networked embedded systems (CAN, Ethernet, LIN, DOIP, ISOTP)

- Familiarity with vehicle diagnostics and common UDS services

- Familiarity with cybersecurity concepts

- Experience with TCP/IP systems, IPv4/6, HTTP/Rest, gRPC

- Experience with systems engineering analysis tools (FMEA, DFMEA, HARA)

- Experience with industry tools such as Canalyzer, PCAN-Explorer, Wireshark

In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. Learn more about our global benefit programs . 

External candidates can apply for this role through the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies careers site ( https://rivianvw.tech/#careers ). If you are a current employee, please apply through our internal job board .

title: Senior Technical Project Manager
description:
Application Modernization Platform (“AMP”) is a MongoDB offering that modernises our customer’s legacy relational applications to a modern architecture underpinned by MongoDB using a combination of software, processes, and engineers. In this offering, the people and software are inextricably linked and cannot be separated. The delivery happens in an accelerated timeframe wherein the team takes advantage of GenAI and algorithmic tooling to expedite the turnaround time for application delivery. 

AMP team generally works with enterprise-grade customers, in all verticals on a variety of exciting use cases. This role solves technically sophisticated problems, gains incredible cross-stack experience, works with top-notch people in the business, addresses multiple customer-facing opportunities. The role also becomes the forefront of groundbreaking R&D that enables further acceleration for enterprises working across a variety of technologies.

AMP exists to expedite time to value for customers who are looking forward to changing, modernising and updating their tech stack while keeping MongoDB the cornerstone of their system architecture.

As the Senior Technical Project Manager, you will work in conjunction with the team’s Technical Lead to lead a small Agile team responsible for migrating a customer’s legacy Java application to a modern cloud-based architecture running on MongoDB. The team will use the latest genAI tools and approaches to accelerate the migration process. You will also be responsible for liaising with customers and internal stakeholders, managing concerns and potential resolutions, and guiding the team towards success. The Agile team will be required to be innovative in deriving solutions to unseen challenges, and you will foster a culture of innovation and collaboration within the team. 

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Germany for our hybrid working model.

Position Expectations

- Agile mindset with an understanding of SCRUM/Kanban processes

- Able to support a project team consisting of onsite, co-located and remote team members

- Be able to proactively identify and remove impediments

- Manage project risks and issues

- Define and refine project team’s “Way of Working”

- Streamline communications between the project team and project stakeholders

- Able to manage expectations of project stakeholders, where the majority are leaders within the organization

- Operate in a small, dynamic, fast-growing team, able to be self-sufficient with an ability to have a can-do attitude and make oneself accountable

- Act as a liaison between the customer, project team and the rest of MongoDB (sales, customer success, support, product and engineering) throughout an engagement

- Create plans and priorities for both project delivery and customer resources. Guide customer as well as project team members to a successful business outcome by managing the client relationship and setting and managing customer expectations during implementations 

- Establish and lead recurring project status or governance meetings, including preparation of materials and working with customer project manager and key internal and external stakeholders to review key project information and maintain visibility and accountability

- Periodically report, in a concise and actionable manner, project status both internally as well as to the customer and document project progress as per established best practices (meeting minutes, project plan updates, weekly status reports)

- Manage escalations or critical situation

- Assist with scoping of solution and project scope definition

- Adopt a consultative and prescriptive approach that inspires trust and confidence

- Be intrigued by the possibilities of genAI to assist in accelerating the delivery of projects

Requirements

- 10+ years of project management experience with enterprise-scale software solutions, large-scale software engineering or consulting services delivery experience preferred

- Excellent customer interaction and presentation skills (ability to present to different audiences and bring the message across in a concise, professional manner) 

- Demonstrated belief in the power of stakeholder management and communications; track record of affecting change through stakeholder engagement

- Services delivery experience with development or operation teams is a plus

- Ability to travel and work on customer sites for a number of continuous weeks

Nice-to-have skills

- Experience as a SCRUM master

- Experience in managing projects with a high degree of uncertainty (research and innovation)

- Experience in delivering software development projects (ideally modernization of a legacy application)

- Experience with JIRA / Project tools

Successful candidates will engage with customer systems and may be exposed to highly confidential customer data, including but not limited to non-public information. For this reason, and due to the nature of the highly regulated industry in which our customers operate, successful candidates may be subject to enhanced background checks, security screenings, and possible constraints around the trading of securities. Successful candidates will understand these requirements and be willing to participate in enhanced screenings and constraints as required by MongoDB and its customers in connection with this role. 

About MongoDB

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB’s unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we’re powering the next era of software.

Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It’s what makes us MongoDB. 

To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we’re committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy , we value our employees’ wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Learn more about what it’s like to work at MongoDB , and help us make an impact on the world!

title: (Senior) Influencer Marketing Manager DACH (m/w/d)
description:
DAS IST DER JOB 

Location: Deutschland (Remote möglich) 

Wir sind everdrop – eine schnell wachsende D2C Brand mit der Mission, die Welt der Haushalts- und Pflegeprodukte nachhaltig zu verändern. Bei uns ist Influencer Marketing kein „Add-on“, sondern einer unserer wichtigsten Wachstumstreiber. Als (Senior) Influencer Marketing Manager (m/w/d) trägst du den Großteil unseres monatlichen Creator-Spends im sechsstelligen Bereich und bist die strategische und analytische Instanz für unser gesamtes Creator-Portfolio. Du entscheidest gemeinsam mit deinem Team Lead, wo wir investieren, was wir skalieren und was wir stoppen. Dabei nutzt du deine Creator-Beziehungen, Daten und KI, um neue Standards für unser Team zu setzen. 

Als (Senior) Influencer Marketing Manager (m/w/d) bei everdrop werden das deine Hauptaufgaben sein: 

- Budget- & Portfolio-Ownership: Du verantwortest den Großteil unseres monatlichen Kooperationsbudgets im sechsstelligen Bereich eigenständig. Du steuerst ein hochvolumiges Portfolio aus Always-on-Creatorn, Performance-Partnern und Top-Creatorn und allokierst Budgets nach CAC, NC ROAS und Skalierungspotenzial. Du bist bereit, Budgets konsequent umzuschichten, wenn die Zahlen es verlangen. 

- Datenanalyse auf Expertenniveau: Du analysierst die Performance über den gesamten Funnel, von CPM und CTR über CVR und AOV bis zu CAC, NC ROAS und LTV. Du baust Dashboards und Forecasts selbst und kannst jederzeit belegen, warum eine Kooperation performt hat oder nicht. Deine Analysen sind die Grundlage für Budgetentscheidungen im Management. 

- Creator-Beziehungen & Verhandlung: Du bringst ein belastbares Netzwerk aus Creatorn und Management-Agenturen mit und baust es weiter aus. Du führst anspruchsvolle Vertrags- und Rahmenverhandlungen mit Top-Creatorn und Agenturen und entwickelst Vergütungsmodelle für nachhaltig hohen NC ROAS und langfristige Partnerschaften. 

- Kreatives Testing mit System: Du denkst in Hypothesen und isolierst Variablen sauber. Du planst Testing-Roadmaps für Produkte, Hooks, Formate und Angles, wertest sie statistisch belastbar aus und überführst die Learnings in Briefings, Bundles und Landingpages. 

- KI als Hebel und neuer Standard: Du setzt KI dort ein, wo sie Qualität und Geschwindigkeit steigert, zum Beispiel bei Creator-Scouting und -Scoring, Performance-Auswertung, Briefing-Erstellung oder Content-Analyse. Du entwickelst daraus Workflows und Best Practices, die das ganze Team nutzt, und hinterfragst bestehende Prozesse kritisch. 

- Konzeption, Bundles & Verkaufspsychologie: Du übersetzt Daten in messerscharfe, kreative Creator-Briefings, konzipierst unwiderstehliche Produkt-Bundles und gestaltest Landingpages mit, gezielt mit verkaufspsychologischen Triggern für maximale Conversion. 

- Schnittstelle zum Performance-Team: Du bist der verlängerte Arm von Paid Media. Du erkennst, welcher Creator-Content als Ad auf Meta oder TikTok performt, sicherst die nötigen Nutzungsrechte und lieferst dem Team laufend frisches Creative-Futter. 

- Channel-Expansion: Du bringst neue Plattformen und Formate in den Mix und baust sie datenbasiert auf. Gerade Social Commerce wie TikTok Shop (Affiliate-Programm, Live-Shopping) ist für uns ein spannendes Feld. 

- Sparring & Standards: Du bist Sparringspartner:in für Management und Kolleg:innen, coachst bei Bedarf Junior-Kolleg:innen und hilfst, Prozesse, Benchmarks und Reportings im Team zu professionalisieren. 

DAS BIST DU 

Du hast Lust in einem Unternehmen zu arbeiten, das sich für einen nachhaltigeren Lifestyle einsetzt? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig. Du übernimmst gerne Verantwortung von Tag 1, gehst Herausforderungen proaktiv an und fühlst dich in einem schnelllebigen und dynamischen Startup-Umfeld wohl? Wir glauben, das könnte ein gutes Match sein! 

Bei everdrop arbeiten Menschen mit Growth Mindset, die Lust darauf haben, immer wieder Neues zu lernen. Wenn du gerne eigene Ideen einbringst, Lust hast, Dinge von Beginn an mitzugestalten und die folgenden Skills und Erfahrungen mitbringst, könnte das der Anfang einer wunderbaren Love Story sein. 

Was du mitbringen solltest:

- Senior-Vorerfahrung: Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung im performance-getriebenen Influencer Marketing in einem schnell wachsenden D2C-E-Commerce-Umfeld oder einer Performance-Agentur, davon mehrere Jahre mit eigener Budgetverantwortung. 

- Budget-Verantwortung: Du hast bereits einen Großteil eines monatlichen Creator-Spends im sechsstelligen Bereich eigenverantwortlich gesteuert und kannst nachweisen, welchen Impact deine Entscheidungen hatten. 

- KI-Kompetenz: Du hast KI bereits praktisch im Marketing eingesetzt, etwa für Analyse, Automatisierung oder Content-Prozesse, und kannst Beispiele nennen, wie du damit Ergebnisse verbessert oder Zeit gespart hast. 

- Analytische Exzellenz: CAC, NC ROAS, CVR, CPM und LTV sind dein Alltag. Du kannst komplexe Performance-Daten über den gesamten Funnel hinweg eigenständig auswerten, Zusammenhänge erkennen, bevor andere sie sehen, und daraus klare Budgetentscheidungen ableiten. Du hinterfragst Zahlen kritisch, trennst Korrelation von Kausalität und stellst deine Erkenntnisse so dar, dass auch das Management sofort handeln kann. 

- Netzwerk: Du bringst bestehende Beziehungen zu Creatorn und Agenturen im DACH-Raum und idealerweise darüber hinaus mit, sodass wir schnell Zugang zu starken Partner:innen bekommen. 

- Verhandlungsgeschick: Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung mit komplexen Verträgen und Rahmenvereinbarungen mit Top-Creatorn und Management-Agenturen. 

- A/B-Testing-Mindset: Du isolierst Variablen, denkst in Hypothesen und leitest daraus klare Handlungsempfehlungen ab. 

- Konsumentenverständnis: Du kennst Direct-Response-Prinzipien und weißt, welche psychologischen Trigger Conversions auslösen, im Storytelling der Creator ebenso wie auf der Landingpage. 

- Ownership: Du verbindest strategisches Denken mit Durchschlagskraft, übernimmst Verantwortung für deine KPIs und behältst auch bei hoher Kampagnendichte den Überblick. 

- Sprachen: Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau (mind. C1) und sichere Englischkenntnisse. Französisch, Italienisch und Polnisch sind ein Plus. 

- Plus: Erfahrung mit TikTok Shop (Affiliate, Live-Shopping, GMV-Tracking). 

DAS IST EVERDROP 

Unsere Mission 💚🌱🌎 

Wir wollen die Welt verändern – gemeinsam mit dir! Die Alltagsprodukte von everdrop helfen den Menschen, ganz einfach ihren ökologischen Fußabdruck im Haushalt zu reduzieren. Im Jahr 2020 sind wir mit unseren Reiniger-Tabs gestartet. Why Deliveroo? 

Our mission is to transform the way people shop and eat, connecting consumers, restaurants, shops, and riders to bring the neighbourhood to their door. We're redefining convenience by giving customers the ability to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.

Deliveroo is a technology-driven company at the forefront of one of the world's most dynamic industries. We are a relatively small team making a very large impact, moving fast, valuing ownership, and tackling some of the most interesting challenges in global commerce. We're driven by innovation, autonomy, and the ambition to deliver exceptional experiences for our customers, partners, and riders alike.

What You'll Be Doing 

You will own frontline operational performance across two closely linked parts of Deliveroo's customer support network: an in-house Global Escalations team of around 50 agents based across the UK and Georgia, and the outsourced network delivering support on our behalf through three BPO partners and three Shared Service Centres, circa 1,500 agents across multiple locations, including the team leads and ops managers embedded within those outsourced functions.

Global Escalations sits at the heart of Deliveroo's most critical customer moments. The team manages our most sensitive, high-risk, and high-impact contacts, including complaints escalated to the Executive team. As the leader directly accountable for this recovery-focused centre of excellence, you will ensure the team operates with exceptional skill, judgement, and empathy, protecting Deliveroo's reputation, driving improvement through root cause analysis, and embedding a culture of integrity and customer-first recovery across the organisation.

For the outsourced network, you own how performance is delivered day to day, working closely with the team leads and ops managers embedded in each BPO and Shared Service Centre, not just the vendor relationship at arm's length. You own the operational rigour needed to make the network the best in class, from an experience and consistency perspective, across every market it supports.

Your key objective is to drive qualitative improvements to the customer experience, measured through CSAT, while balancing cost metrics like average handling time (AHT) and refund costs, rather than trading one off against the other. You will be the voice of Support to Deliveroo's market General Managers, taking full accountability for the Support experience in your markets, and you will partner closely with cross-functional Support & Operations teams, including Workforce Management, Training, Quality, and Policy, to drive initiatives that positively impact all three sides of the marketplace: customers, riders, and merchants.

You Will… 

- Own frontline operational performance delivered through the in-house Global Escalations team (UK and Georgia) and the outsourced network (3 BPOs, 3 Shared Service Centres, circa 1,500 agents), including the team leads and ops managers within those outsourced functions

- Lead and develop the Global Escalations team directly, managing our most sensitive and reputation-critical contacts with judgement, empathy, and rigorous root cause analysis

- Drive qualitative improvements to the customer experience, tracked through CSAT, while balancing cost metrics like AHT and refund costs

- Act as the voice of Support to Deliveroo market GMs, taking full accountability for the Support experience in your markets and representing their priorities back into the function

- Partner with Support & Operations cross-functional teams, including Workforce Management, Training, Quality, and Policy, to drive initiatives that improve the experience for customers, riders, and merchants

- Design and run performance frameworks that hold BPO and SSC team leads and ops managers accountable for quality, SLA adherence, and CSAT, fostering a culture of partnership rather than pure oversight

- Standardise processes and playbooks across outsourced partners and sites where it drives consistency, while respecting genuine market and site-specific differences

- Diagnose and help bring down attrition and quality issues across the outsourced network, working with BPO and SSC leadership on the retention, engagement, and workforce planning changes needed

- Partner with Product and Technology to shape the roadmap for customer support systems and channel strategy, identifying opportunities to enhance efficiency and automation across both in-house and outsourced teams

- Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders across HR, Legal, and Policy to ensure service delivery evolves in line with business priorities

- Drive data-informed improvement through analysis of contact drivers, escalation themes, and customer sentiment, translating insight into action for both Global Escalations and the outsourced network

- Represent the function at relevant Weekly Business Reviews and senior forums, providing visibility on performance, risk, and recovery across both the in-house team and the outsourced network

- Participate in the 24/7 Leadership Team on-call rota

- Shape functional strategy and set OKRs for contact centre Support across Deliveroo markets, growing the remit from directing your own team to leading leaders, in line with DoorDash's Team Management career framework

- Grow and develop the managers and leaders within your network, including Team Leads inside Global Escalations and the team leads and ops managers at each BPO and Shared Service Centre, building the next generation of people leaders

Skills & Experience You'll Need 

- Extensive contact centre, BPO, or shared service centre leadership experience in a fast-paced, consumer-facing environment

- Proven experience managing outsourced or vendor relationships at scale, including the team lead and ops manager layer embedded within partner organisations, not just the commercial relationship

- Experience leading escalations or complaint handling in a reputation-sensitive environment, with strong judgement and the ability to drive recovery from the most sensitive customer moments

- A track record of bringing consistency and governance across multiple outsourced partners while respecting genuine local and market differences

- Experience diagnosing and reducing attrition while improving quality, in a large-scale, multi-site support operation

- A data-driven approach to balancing customer experience (CSAT) against cost metrics such as AHT and refund rate, without trading one off blindly against the other

- Experience representing a support or operations function to senior commercial stakeholders, such as General Managers or market leadership, taking full accountability for their experience of the function

- Experience partnering with cross-functional teams such as Workforce Management, Training, Quality, and Policy to drive improvements across a multi-sided marketplace

- Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and work cross-functionally with Product, Legal, Policy, and People teams

- Strong analytical ability, comfortable turning contact driver, escalation, and sentiment data into action

- Strong people leadership skills, with experience building and developing a dispersed in-house team and driving performance indirectly through partner leadership

- A self-starter mindset, a can-do attitude, and willingness to be hands-on in a fast-moving, multi-geography environment

- Proven strategic mindset with a track record of shaping and executing operational strategies across multiple markets and vendors

- Deep operational understanding, including customer service design, vendor management, and process optimisation

- Demonstrated ability to deliver results in high-volume, complex environments with multiple priorities

- Experience partnering with Product and Tech to drive tooling, system, and automation improvements

- A mindset focused on continuous improvement, customer advocacy, and operational excellence

- Demonstrated ability to operate at a 'leads leaders' level per DoorDash's Levels and Expectations framework (Team Management track): shaping strategy and OKRs beyond your own team, and developing managers who in turn develop their own teams

title: Partner Operations Manager
description:
Location: Our offices are in Central London, along with several of our customers. Travel to our customer sites is required, the frequency of which will vary from customer-to-customer. You need to be able to travel onsite to London up to 3 days per week, although onsite requirements will vary week-to-week and customer-to-customer from 0 to 3 days.

Salary: £30,000-£40,000

SC Clearance Requirements: 

Due to working with several government bodies, SC clearance is required for all our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance . In future, DV clearance may be required, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

You must be UK-based .

About us 

We help major public and private sector organisations scale cloud and AI with speed, control and clarity. Hard-won experience sits behind a values-led business that does the right thing, puts customers first and builds partnerships on trust rather than lock-in.

Our work is practical. We design secure, production-ready foundations that hold up in the real world and deliver lasting value, without the waste that slows most transformations down. And we don't advise from the sidelines. We build, fix and deliver ourselves, with no offshoring, no resource-padding and no compromises.

What you'll do 

Cloudscaler works closely with three of the companies shaping cloud and AI right now: AWS, Anthropic and OpenAI. Those partnerships open real doors for us and our customers. Funding for customer programmes. Early access to new models and services. Joint go-to-market. But they only pay off when someone runs them properly. That's this role.

You'll own the operational side of our partner programmes. Your goals are clear: help us win partner funding for our customers, achieve new AWS competencies and programme designations, and keep our partner CRMs in excellent shape. The partner managers at AWS, Anthropic and OpenAI will know you by name.

This isn't a back-office admin job. AI partner programmes change quarter to quarter, and we want someone who'll build smarter ways of running them. If you've ever automated a tedious task because you couldn't face doing it by hand a second time, you'll fit right in.

External responsibilities 

These responsibilities are partner-facing and customer-facing:

Competencies and programme designations - Driving our AWS competency and programme applications, and tracking tier requirements, certifications and renewals across AWS, Anthropic and OpenAI so that nothing lapses.

Partner funding applications - Preparing, submitting and tracking partner funding applications (for example the AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP) and proof-of-concept funding), working with our sales and delivery teams to gather what each one needs.

Funding claims - Managing funding claims through to payment, keeping milestones, evidence and deadlines in order.

Partner relationships - Acting as the main operational contact for our partner teams, building strong working relationships with each company.

Joint campaigns and events - Helping plan and run joint marketing campaigns with our partners, and representing Cloudscaler at partner events across the UK.

Internal responsibilities 

These responsibilities cover the systems, reporting and ways of working behind our partner programmes.

Partner CRMs - Owning our partner CRMs, keeping deal registrations, opportunity data and partner portals accurate across HubSpot and AWS Partner Central.

Reporting - Reporting on partner performance, funding pipeline and programme health to the leadership team.

Automation - Finding the repetitive work and automating it, using AI tools such as Claude to build workflows, trackers and agents that give the team time back.

Briefing colleagues - Briefing colleagues when programmes change, and explaining what it means for our customers and bids.

What we're looking for 

This is an operational role with plenty of partner contact. We expect candidates to demonstrate the following:

Operational experience - Experience in partner operations, alliance management, programme management or a similar operational role, ideally in tech or professional services.

Attention to detail - A sharp eye for detail. You notice when a date, a figure or a requirement doesn't add up, and you fix it before it costs anyone.

Communication - Clear, confident communication in writing and in person, with colleagues, partners and senior stakeholders.

Organisation - Strong organisation across many moving parts and competing deadlines.

Systems - Comfort with CRM systems (HubSpot ideally) and spreadsheets.

Curiosity about AI - Genuine curiosity about AI. You already use tools like Claude or ChatGPT to work faster, and you want to go further.

Partner programme knowledge - Experience with AWS partner programmes or cloud funding is a real advantage, but not essential. We'll teach you the specifics.

Why this role 

We hire people who are curious and like to tinker. The people who thrive in this role will be the ones who see a messy process and can't resist building something better, then can explain it to the rest of the team with real enthusiasm. You'll work directly with three of the companies shaping cloud and AI, and as the partner programmes grow, so will the role, with real room to develop your career here.

Benefits 

- Periodic offer of share options schemes

- Discretionary bonus scheme

- 25 days’ annual leave + 5 additional days for training/exams or volunteering

- Travel and accommodation expensed where eligible in line with our expenses policy

- Life Assurance

- Long Term Disability cover

Drive AI and automation for outbound and inbound 

- Partner with the GTM Engineering team, who own Clay and the AI automation for SDRs, and act as the business owner of the SDR automation roadmap, defining the use cases and priorities for AI-driven outbound: signal-based targeting, account and contact research, enrichment, personalisation, and sequencing.

title: Technical Writer, Frontier AI Best Practice
description:
About the AI Security Institute

The AI Security Institute is the world's largest and best-funded team dedicated to understanding advanced AI risks and translating that knowledge into action. We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.

We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.

The deadline for applying to this role is Sunday 29th November 2026, end of day, anywhere on Earth. 

About the team 

AISI's Technical Standards and Best Practice team identifies what best practice is needed to manage the most serious risks from frontier AI development and leverages AISI’s position to get it adopted. 

AI capabilities are advancing faster than the science and practices used to manage their risks. Risks now emerge earlier, during training, internal deployment and evaluation, not just at public release, and evaluation methods are struggling to keep pace. Yet there is no consensus on the set of practices needed to safely use and develop the most capable AI systems, and high-level principles are not enough to manage these risks. What's needed is concrete technical guidance that developers agree is necessary. 

AISI is uniquely placed to lead on parts of this industry-wide effort to establish best practice. We house researchers with state-of-the-art technical insight on keeping AI secure during internal use, hold existing relationships with industry and other frontier AI organisations, and offer a neutral third-party home to establish best practice collaboratively. This role directly delivers on part of the Prime Minister’s September 2026 commitment that the UK will work towards principles and standards that ensure the most capable AI systems are developed securely and with appropriate transparency. It builds directly on our October 2026 publication Towards technical best practice for frontier AI development , setting out our view of the most urgent priorities. 

This is a new, growing team with high ambitions. It is a cross AISI initiative that draws on and collaborates with researchers and engineers from across AISI's research teams, as well as our Communications, International and Strategy teams. We're now building a dedicated core team and expect it to grow as the work does. 

Why this team matters: 

AISI is uniquely placed to shape this guidance, and this team is how we'll do it: 

- Technical expertise: AISI has roughly 10 technical and research teams whose expertise can be drawn on; one of the largest groups working on AI risk outside the frontier AI companies. AISI has evaluated more than 55 frontier models before release and published research on topics such as safety cases, monitorability and control. 

- A research institute within government: we work directly with leading AI developers, other governments , and third-party evaluators, and can bring them together around practices no single company would set on its own. UK AISI also coordinates the International Network for Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science – a group of 10 AI security institutes and equivalents – which has already published its own and socialised others’ best practices. 

- A track record of shaping industry practice: AISI has already helped establish voluntary practices such as pre-release testing, and built Inspect, now the standard framework for leading third-party evaluators. 

We're not seeking to mandate requirements. We want to contribute our expertise to an industry-wide effort to develop technical best practice that could later inform formal standards. 

What we're working on: 

Examples of our first priority areas include: 

- Overseeing AI systems: what monitoring and controls developers need to make sure AI systems behave as intended, and how to preserve that oversight as systems become more capable. 

- Sharing information on the speed of AI development: which metrics best track progress, including AI's use in its own development, and when they should be shared with governments and the public. 

- Assessing and documenting risk: what risk assessments and safety cases should cover, and what standard of evidence they should meet. 

About the role 

Primary objective: turn AISI's technical expertise into authoritative best-practice documents that frontier AI developers find valuable and use, and into clear explanations of why those practices matter. 

You'll work closely with AISI researchers and the standards team on two kinds of writing. 

Example responsibilities: 

- 
Best-practice documents (about 50%) 

- Work with researchers to decide what form each piece of best practice should take, and how it should be structured. 

- Own delivery of best-practice documents, co-drafting by managing researchers’ technical input and editing to ensure each practice is coherent, specific, testable and technically accurate. 

- Set out the technical rationale for each practice, drawing on research findings, threat models and evaluation results, so the case for it is evidence-based and credible to a diverse set of expert readers. 

- Develop a consistent style, templates and terminology for AISI best practice documents, and run review rounds with internal and external experts. 

- 
Explainers (about 50%) 

- Write public explainers and technical blog posts setting out the reasoning behind AISI's best practice: why it matters, and what it means for developers, policymakers and the public. For example, the series that follow our agenda, Towards technical best practice for frontier AI development. 

- Manage multi-stakeholder drafting processes, engaging with feedback from industry, wider government and expert third parties. 

- Adapt material for different audiences, from technical researchers to non-technical policy readers, working with AISI's communications team. 

Reporting and growth: 

You'll report to the Head of Technical Standards and Best Practice. This role by default has no line management responsibilities thought responsibility will scale as the team grows . You'll learn from AISI's researchers across a wide range of frontier AI safety topics, and help shape a new team as it grows. 

What we are looking for 

We're flexible on the exact profile and expect successful candidates will meet many, but not necessarily all, of the criteria below. This role is most likely to fall at Level 4, but we are open to exceptional candidates at other levels . 

Essential: 

We're looking for someone who can: 

- Understand nuanced technical AI safety work well enough to explain its claims and limitations accurately, 

- Write precise, structured documents that set out what organisations should do and why, 

- Explain the same technical topics clearly and engagingly to non-technical readers 

For example, you might have: 

- Written or co-written AI research papers, such as preprints on arXiv. 

- Written in-depth technical communication on AI working directly with researchers, such as AI company blog posts or technical reports. 

- Written technical guidance, standards or documentation in a complex field. 

- Written for public or policy audiences on technical topics. 

You don't need all of these. For a sense of the level and style we're looking for, see the work our research teams publish on the AISI blog by our research teams. 

Desirable: 

- Familiarity with one or more of our priority areas: monitorability, safety cases and risk reports, or AI research automation. 

- Extensive experience communicating AI security concepts for policy audiences. 

- Experience running the writing of a multi-author document: gathering input from several experts, resolving conflicting feedback and getting it to publication. 

- Familiarity with how frontier AI developers, evaluators or standards bodies work, for example from working at or alongside them. 

Example backgrounds: 

- An AI safety researcher who has published several papers and especially enjoys the writing and framing side of research. 

- A technical writer or science communicator with a machine learning degree or AI background, who has co-written papers or reports on AI research. 

- A research engineer or analyst at an AI safety organisation who has led writing on published frameworks or reports. 

Core requirements 

- You should be able to spend at least 4 days per week working with us. 

- No security clearance is needed to apply. Eligibility for Security Check (SC) clearance is preferred, but not essential. More detail on clearance eligibility can be found on the UK Government website: National security vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK. 

Interview process

Candidates should expect to go through some or all of the following stages once an application has been submitted: 

- Initial interview 

- Technical take home test 

- Second interview and review of take home test 

- Third interview 

- Final interview with members of the senior team 

What We Offer 

Impact you couldn't have anywhere else 

- Incredibly talented, mission-driven and supportive colleagues. 

- Direct influence on how frontier AI is governed and deployed globally. 

- Work with the Prime Minister’s AI Advisor and leading AI companies. 

- Opportunity to shape the first & best-resourced public-interest research team focused on AI security. 

Resources & access 

- Pre-release access to multiple frontier models and ample compute. 

- Extensive operational support so you can focus on research and ship quickly. 

- Work with experts across national security, policy, AI research and adjacent sciences. 

Growth & autonomy 

- If you’re talented and driven, you’ll own important problems early. 

- 5 days off and annual stipends for learning and development, and funding for conferences and external collaborations. 

- Freedom to pursue research bets without product pressure. 

- Opportunities to publish and collaborate externally. 

Life & family* 

- Modern central London office, or where applicable, option to work in similar government offices in Birmingham, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, Salford or Bristol. 

- Hybrid working, flexibility for occasional remote work abroad and stipends for work-from-home equipment. 

- At least 25 days’ annual leave, 8 public holidays, extra team-wide breaks and 3 days off for volunteering. 

- Generous paid parental leave (36 weeks of UK statutory leave shared between parents + 3 extra paid weeks + option for additional unpaid time). 

- On top of your salary, we contribute 28.97% of your base salary to your pension. 

- Discounts and benefits for cycling to work, donations and retail/gyms.

London ( Hybrid) | Technology & Engineering | Permanent 

The Role 

As a Principal Security Engineer at Capco, you'll lead hands-on security engineering delivery for clients across financial services and other complex environments. Depending on the engagement, you'll lead a technical workstream or operate independently as a Principal specialist. Your focus will span Application & Product Security, Cloud & Platform Security and DevSecOps, underpinned by strong security automation. You'll combine specialist depth with cross-domain judgement, client engagement and secure-by-design engineering. 

What You'll Do 

- Lead the design, implementation and technical assurance of secure solutions across applications, cloud platforms and delivery pipelines; remain hands-on with complex engineering and integration challenges. 

- Work directly with clients to understand requirements, lead technical workshops and shape practical security designs, delivery plans and technical proposals. 

- Embed security-by-design across applications, APIs, cloud workloads and the secure SDLC through threat modelling, CI/CD controls, SAST, SCA, DAST and container scanning. 

- Build and integrate scalable security automation using scripting, APIs, Infrastructure as Code and policy as code; improve control effectiveness and engineering workflows. 

- Lead technical workstreams or specialist assignments, assure engineering quality and operational handover, mentor engineers and develop reusable standards and patterns. 

- Leverage approved AI-enabled tools and automation to enhance security engineering efficiency and effectiveness, ensuring appropriate human oversight, security guardrails and validation. 

What We're Looking For 

- Proven hands-on security engineering delivery and technical leadership, including secure design decisions, engineering assurance, client engagement and mentoring. 

- Deep implementation expertise in one or more of Application & Product Security, Cloud & Platform Security or DevSecOps , with working knowledge of the other areas. 

- Practical experience securing applications, APIs, cloud workloads or engineering pipelines, supported by sound knowledge of threat modelling, vulnerability management and secure SDLC practices. 

- Experience with at least one major cloud platform (Azure, AWS or GCP) and cloud-native security principles, including an understanding of IaC , containers and workload identities. 

- Strong security automation capability with scripting, APIs and CI/CD tooling, plus experience with IaC or policy as code and integrating security tools into engineering workflows. 

- Broad awareness of network and infrastructure security, IAM, monitoring and data-protection controls; able to collaborate with specialists and explain technical trade-offs to clients. 

- Strong understanding of security standards and best practices, including ISO 27001, NIST and OWASP, with the ability to translate security requirements into practical engineering controls and solutions. 

Bonus Points For 

- Experience in financial services, energy or other regulated sectors; relevant certifications such as CISSP, CSSLP, CCSP or cloud security credentials. 

- Depth across multiple priority engineering domains; experience in software supply-chain or container security, technical presales, or security engineering for AI-enabled systems. 

Why Join Capco 

- Deliver high-impact security engineering solutions for leading financial institutions and other major clients. 

- Work in a collaborative, entrepreneurial consulting culture with continuous learning, training and certification opportunities 

- Help shape secure digital transformation across financial services and energy. 

Benefits 

We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life: 

- Core Benefits: Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover. 

- Mental Health: Easy access to CareFirst, Unmind, Aviva consultations, and in-house first aiders. 

- Family-Friendly: Maternity, adoption, shared parental leave, plus paid leave for sickness, pregnancy loss, fertility treatment, menopause, and bereavement. 

- Family Care: Eight complimentary backup care sessions for emergency childcare or elder care. 

- Holiday Flexibility: Five weeks of annual leave with the option to buy or sell holiday days based on your needs. 

- Continuous Learning: Minimum 40 hours of training annually through workshops, certifications, and e-learning. You'll also be assigned a Business Coach from Day One to support your professional development. 

- Healthcare Access: Convenient online GP services. 

- Extra Perks: Wellhub ( Gympass ), travel insurance, Tastecard , season ticket loans, Cycle to Work, and dental insurance. 

Inclusion at Capco 

We're committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know - we'll be happy to help. 

We value each person's unique perspective and contribution. At Capco, we believe that being yourself is your greatest strength. Our #BeYourselfAtWork culture encourages individuality and collaboration - a mindset that shapes how we work with clients and each other every day. 

#LI-DNI

title: Product Manager - Snacks
description:
Vilgain makes high-quality food - clean, functional ingredients, no shortcuts, no filler additives . 

We're 700+ people across Prague, Brno and London, already selling in 12+ markets across Europe, the UK, the US and beyond. 
We're on a mission to change how people think about food , and we're growing fast to do it - expanding internationally and building a company where people have a real say in what we make and how we make it, not just a seat at the table. 

Your mission 🎯 

You'll own specific product development projects from brief to launch, working directly with third-party suppliers and manufacturers. Working closely with the Category Manager, you'll make sure every project is aligned with the wider category goals and launch plan, and spot the commercial opportunities that will help the category grow. 

What will you do? 

- Owning end-to-end new product development projects, from initial brief through development to market launch. 

- Running projects with third-party manufacturers – sourcing and selecting suppliers and managing those relationships day to day. 

- Reporting into the Category Manager and making sure your projects are aligned with the wider category goals and launch plan. 

- Building the commercial case for your projects – costings, margins and volumes – and prioritising the opportunities with the highest value. 

- Partnering with design, marketing, Regulatory and QA to bring products to market, including briefs, documentation and artwork sign-off. 

- Running existing product development (EPD) projects such as product improvements, packaging amends and label corrections. 

- Monitoring market trends and identifying new commercial opportunities for the category. 

What do we expect from you? 

- At least 3 years' experience in NPD, project management or a similar role in the food industry – food experience is essential. 

- Experience with private label production and working with third-party manufacturers. 

- Highly numerate and financially aware, with the commercial sense to prioritise high-value opportunities. 

- Experience in a small business or startup environment – we move quickly, and you'll need to be happy with the fast pace of a rapidly growing business. 

- Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to juggle several projects at once. 

- A proactive problem-solver who takes initiative and can work independently. 

- A strong communicator who can build good relationships with colleagues, both internally and externally. 

- Confident with spreadsheets and project management tools, and actively uses AI tools to work smarter. 

- A love for food and a genuine interest in making a difference to the food system. 

- Fluent in English.

What we offer: 

- Based in London, hybrid – minimum 3 days a week in the office. 

- Fast-paced, growing team where your work has a visible impact on the products we launch. 

- 5 weeks of vacation, flexible hours, and remote work options, get monthly shopping credits. 

- Stay connected through team events, breakfasts, and group workouts.

title: Senior Pricing Analyst, B2B
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Most delivery companies sell on price and volume, and find out later whether a client made them money. Sales teams are measured on what they sign, not on what a signing is worth. Relay wants every client, and every new shop in the network, to be one we'd choose again.

That is harder for us than for most, because what a client is worth depends on how their parcels flow through a network that's still growing. Engineering and analytics engineering build what you design.

Sales Highlights

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide what a client or shop is worth and which signings sales should chase. The sales lead acts on your calls.

- What is a new client or a new shop worth, when its value depends on where it sits in a network that changes every month? What would you build so sales knows before it signs?

- Which signings become partners who do well with us, and what does that tell sales to look for?

- The quarter's target is set. What has to close by when for it to hold, and what would tell you early that it won't?

- A whole area, not a slice: you decide how sales values what it wins, and the result shows in what we sign next.

- Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Pricing Analyst, B2B at Relay, you'll:

- Decide which Sales problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.

- Design how Sales decides: which signals count, what a client or shop is worth, and what good looks like.

- Tell the sales lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.

- Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.

- Go and look when the numbers and the street disagree: a new shop, a client's parcels at the sort centre.

- Get the missing data built, and prove whether each change worked. In a year, sales chooses what to go after on measures you built, and can see whether the quarter will land before it ends.

We're looking for candidates who…

- Have owned B2B pricing or commercial decisions and their number, rather than maintaining sales dashboards.

- Have built, hands on, the first version of how a company values a customer or a deal: unit economics, lifetime value, or what it costs to win one.

- Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or sales went after different deals because of it.

- Have got records created by teams who didn't report to you, and know how long it takes.

- Can say early whether a quarter will land, and what would tell you it won't.

- Are hands-on and fluent in SQL, with or without AI, and would rather ship a working answer this week than a perfect one next quarter. No logistics experience needed, just the appetite to learn a physical operation fast.

Don't tick every box? If this problem excites you, we'd still love to hear from you. 

Who Thrives at Relay? 

- Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

- Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

- 1% Better Every Day : You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

- All In, All the Time : You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

- People-Powered Greatness : You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

- Grow the Whole Pie : You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. THE TEAM
• ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Parcel delivery has a quality problem the industry has learned to live with. Parcels go missing between depots. Parcels get marked as delivered and never reach the customer. Most carriers treat a steady rate of loss as a cost of doing business. Relay is building the delivery company where that stops being true.

That is harder for us than for most, because nearly everyone who touches a Relay parcel is an independent partner. We can't manage them into performance. We have to build the standards, the evidence and the product that make doing the job well the natural outcome. Engineering builds the product changes you design.

Partner Excellence Highlights

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide which signals count, which checks become rules, and whether each fix belongs in product, policy or training. The squad lead acts on your calls.

- Most of a parcel's journey happens between scans. How do you prove a handover happened without making the job slower for the people doing it?

- A delivery is marked complete and the customer says it never came. How do you tell a wrong address from a handover that went wrong, and put the fix where it belongs: product, policy or training?

- Some checks can only answer "can't tell". Which are worth making provable, and which should we stop measuring?

- A whole area, not a slice: you decide what evidence a whole network runs on, and the result is on the street the next morning.

- Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

The Opportunity

title: Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
description:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. 

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

🎯 The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product.

You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own.

You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another.

🧩 The problem you would be working on

Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence.

OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost.

Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one.

OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable.

🛠️ What you would work on

- End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome.

- The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability.

- The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation.

- Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows.

- The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions.

🏆 What success could look like

Priorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have:

- Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users.

- Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it.

- Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible.

- Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle.

- Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them.

- Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on.

🌐 Open source, like the rest of Filigran

OpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it.

👥 The squad

You will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation.

You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows.

✨ What will help you succeed

We do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions.

- A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need.

- Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design.

- The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve.

- Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time.

- Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification.

- Fluent English is required. 

💡 Useful, but not required

Any of the following would help, but none is expected:

- Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification.

- Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks.

- Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP.

⚙️ The stack

TypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo.

OpenCRQ ships as a container, both as SaaS and on customer-managed infrastructure. We use OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs, alongside Prometheus and continuous profiling.

A significant part of the design work happens at the boundaries between OpenCRQ, the rest of Filigran’s product suite and customer security tooling. You will work directly with the teams that own those systems rather than having to navigate those boundaries alone.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job. 

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company , and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation . You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger 

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next 

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders 

Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.

🧭 A culture grounded in CORE

Husky is what we call the distributed, petabyte-scale columnar event store at the heart of our Event Platform, which powers dozens of Datadog’s most popular products – Logs, RUM, APM , Cloud Network Monitoring, Netflow, and many more. Husky was built from the ground up at Datadog to store and query massive volumes of event data at low cost, with data fully queryable within seconds of arrival.

As an Engineering Manager on Husky, you will lead one of a few closely collaborating teams that work directly on Husky’s internals. We own the full lifecycle of events stored by our Event Platform – whether it’s managing the ingestion of over 100 million events per second exactly-once , optimizing the persistence layer with lightning-fast compaction , tweaking our columnar format, timely deletion across hundreds of thousands of customer tables, or building the metadata service that enables hundreds of thousands of queries per second – you will be responsible for the growth and success of a team constantly meeting new scalability requirements driven by Datadog’s growing customer base and suite of products. 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. 

What You’ll Do: 

- 
Manage a team of software engineers ranging from new grads to senior engineers, focusing on career development, inclusivity, and high impact

- 
Be a technical leader of the team; while the role may not involve frequent hands on coding, you’ll be reviewing architecture decisions, RFCs, and pull requests and ensuring what the team ships is high quality

- 
Partner with product teams to evaluate use cases, ensure smooth implementation, and prioritize new platform capabilities. 

- 
Share on-call responsibilities with the rest of the team and ensure a culture of operational excellence

- 
Scale a petabyte-scale database to an exabyte-scale one

Who You Are: 

- 
A software engineer at heart with previous experience leading software engineering teams and a track record of delivering high-quality software products, preferably with some hands on experience with Java or Go and a background in distributed systems.

- 
Experienced with being on-call, leading incident responses, writing post mortems, and driving remediation efforts

- 
An excellent leader with strong interpersonal skills, with experience in career development and performance management.

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. 

Benefits and Growth: 

- 
New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

title: Manager I, Applied AI - Distilled Models
description:
Applied AI is where Datadog's ambitious AI bets get built and shipped ( Bits Chat , updog ). We sit at the intersection of research and product: turning promising capabilities from Datadog AI Research lab and the research community into production systems that reach real customers. The team builds specialized models that replace frontier models where they are not necessary, making AI capabilities faster, cheaper, and more secure. The mandate is to move fast from idea to customer impact, and when a product finds its footing, to set it up for growth.

As a Manager I in Applied AI, you will lead a team of engineers and applied scientists working on one of these challenges. You will define technical direction, run short feedback loops, make deliberate decisions about what to pursue or stop, and work closely with product managers, research teams, and cross-functional partners to ship AI capabilities that matter.

- Lead and develop a team of engineers and applied scientists focused on cost-efficient specialized models and AI security capabilities

- Own end-to-end delivery of high-quality AI systems, from early research exploration to production-grade reliability, with high standards for operational excellence, system reliability, and technical quality

- Navigate the unique challenges of shipping AI-powered products: balancing quality, latency, cost, and safety considerations.
