description:
WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP 

Details

Preferred starting date: ASAP

Weekly availability: Full-time (5 days/week)

Period: 6 months

Location: Aerospace Innovation Hub, Delft, the Netherlands

About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced onboard UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers who are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members come from different backgrounds such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics, and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub on the TU Delft campus in the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low-TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.

The project 

Sensor calibration is a manual job today, and it does not scale to the number of sensor units we intend to ship. We are building automated test and calibration infrastructure to fix that, starting with a cell built around a UFactory UF850 robotic arm on a linear rail.

We already have the arm and the calibration software. What we do not have is the physical cell around it, or the software that drives it. This first project is split into two internships that run side by side:

• Robot programming and automation — this position

• Mechanical design and integration — separate posting

The two interns will work closely together. Neither half of this project is any good on its own. This calibration cell is the first thing we are building on this front, not the last, so there is a good chance the right person carries on to other robotics and automation projects once it is running.

Your role 

If you are the kind of person who is not satisfied until an automated system actually works reliably, not just once, this internship is designed for you.

We are looking for a Robot Programming & Automation Intern to help build the software behind our robotic test and automation infrastructure. Your first project is turning a robotic arm on a linear rail into a system that reliably captures good calibration data — but the skills involved are the same ones we’ll lean on for whatever we automate next: getting a robot to move well, knowing whether the data it’s collecting is any good, and building something solid enough to run unattended.

Getting that right is the substance of this internship, on this project and on whatever comes after it.

What you’ll do 

• Build the robot control layer: drive the arm through its SDK, coordinate the linear rail, and plan safe motion inside a cell that also has a target, cables, and an operator in it.

• Design pose generation that’s actually informed by the calibration problem, including getting proper coverage across a multi-camera rig rather than just one lens at a time.

• Get the timing and synchronisation right between the robot, the cameras, and the captured data — this is where automated rigs usually go wrong.

• Gate data quality at capture time, and retry within the run rather than finding out later that a dataset is unusable.

• Close the loop with our existing calibration pipeline: feed it data, read back its results, and use that to decide what to capture next and when a run is done.

• Package captures with the metadata needed to make a calibration reproducible, and make the whole thing robust to failures mid-run.

• Build a simple operator-facing workflow: mount the rig, pick a profile, press go.

• Work closely with the mechanical intern — your requirements shape their fixture design, and their measurements shape your motion limits.

Who you are 

• You are enrolled in a relevant study program (Robotics, Computer Science, Computational Science and Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, or similar).

• You are strong in Python. C++ is a plus.

• You are comfortable with 3D geometry: rigid transforms, rotation representations, coordinate frames, and keeping your conventions straight when it is 6pm and nothing lines up.

• You are interested in robot programming specifically — motion, reachability, collisions, repeatability — and not only in the vision maths around it.

• You understand enough about how camera calibration works to reason about what makes a dataset good or useless. You do not need to be able to write the solver.

• You have worked with real sensors and real robots, and you have learned that they lie about timing.

• You care about reliability. An automated process that works four times out of five is not automated.

• You write code that another engineer can pick up and extend.

• You are comfortable taking responsibility for software that moves physical hardware.

• You are independent, curious, organized, and resourceful.

• Linux does not scare you, and neither does a robot that moves the moment your code says move.

We care much more about what you have built and made work than about grades.

Nice to have 

These are strong pluses, but not strict requirements:

• ROS 2, MoveIt 2, tf2, and motion planning in practice

• Experience with industrial or collaborative arm SDKs (UFactory / xArm, UR, Franka), or motion control more generally

• Hands-on camera calibration experience: OpenCV, Kalibr, ChArUco or AprilTag targets, hand-eye calibration

• Multi-camera rigs, and the specific pain of calibrating cameras with little or no overlapping field of view

• Machine vision cameras: triggering and synchronisation, GenICam, exposure control, rolling versus global shutter

• Coverage or observability reasoning: understanding why some poses inform a parameter and others do not

• Simulation environments (Gazebo, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo)

• Docker, CI, and the habit of writing tests before you need them

• Experience turning a research script into something an operator can actually use

Please include 

When applying, please include links, repositories, or writeups that show us you build things that work. For example:

• GitHub repositories, with a note on which parts you actually wrote

• robot arm or robot motion projects

• camera calibration, multi-view geometry, SLAM, or structure-from-motion work

• data capture pipelines, test automation, or anything that had to run unattended

• computer vision projects

• simulation work

• a short writeup of something that broke and how you found the cause

• anything that demonstrates hands-on technical ownership

If you have ever chased a calibration error you couldn’t explain, eventually traced it to a timestamp, and fixed it properly, you’ll probably fit right in.

Requirements 

• Enrolled in a relevant study program (Robotics, Computer Science, CSE, Mechatronics, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, or similar)

• Strong programming skills, Python at minimum

• Comfortable working in Linux

• Strong interest in robotics, automation, computer vision, or perception

• English proficiency

• Organized and proactive working style

What we offer 

• 1000 euro monthly compensation

• 10 vacation days during the internship period

• Flexible working hours and the option to work from home 2 days per week where practical

• A direct and significant influence on highly innovative products

• The opportunity to work close to the hardware and the product, with fast iteration and tight feedback loops

• Full ownership of a self-contained system that the rest of the company will depend on

• A team environment where practical experimentation, learning, and ownership are expected

The application procedure 

• If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself. This can be a resume, website, portfolio, or any other source that gives us a clear impression of your background, technical skills, and hands-on experience.

• We will get back to you ASAP. If we think you could be a fit for the position, we will invite you for an informal introduction so we can get to know you, and equally important, you can get to know us. After this, a more technically focused interview may follow.

title: International Expansion - Netherlands
description:
At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.

Read more about what we’re building here .

We’re looking for a commercially sharp, highly autonomous operator to drive Axle’s commercial success in the Dutch market. 

Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach internationally. Our goal is to become the go-to platform for energy flexibility globally, and we’re hiring the person to make that happen.

This role will assess Axle’s participation in Dutch markets and business models from first principles: diving deep into regulations, modelling revenue-per-asset, and trialling new propositions at pace.

You speak Dutch and fluent English. Other European languages will also be an asset.

What you will be doing 

- Owning Axle’s commercial results in the Dutch market: pipeline, revenue and partner success

- Winning new customers end-to-end, from first conversation through to commercial close, and setting partners up to generate meaningful revenue

- Driving go-to-market execution with partners, including value propositions, pricing, customer segmentation and launch strategy

- Building the zero-to-one of the business through partnerships. You’ll be on the phone (and eventually on the ground) with utilities/retailers, potential clients and grid operators, creating and disproving hypotheses as quickly as possible

- Continuing to sharpen our view of where the value is and which markets and business models are accessible to us

- Building lasting relationships with grid operators and the regulator, so that Axle is well positioned as the market evolves

- Acting as the conduit between partners and engineering, creating fast, structured feedback loops that turn field insights into product improvements

As such, we are looking for a “full-stack operator” who can process highly technical information, ramp up commercial value, and accelerate us into new markets.

You might have previous experience in one or more of the activities above, but we are more interested in your growth potential than your domain-specific expertise. We are looking for people who have built things, developed new relationships, and helped get big projects over the line in complex environments.

This is an opportunity to deliver first-of-a-kind projects in one of Europe’s most important flexibility markets, become a domain expert, and work at the bleeding edge of electrification.

What’s in it for you

This is a 12 month fixed-term contract. Compensation is highly competitive and dependent on experience.

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

You’ll be based in the Netherlands. To maximise collaboration, we ask that you spend ~1 week per month working from our London office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

title: AI Engineer l Young Talent Program
description:
The rules of building are being rewritten. Come write them with us. 

Every few decades, the way companies are built gets reinvented from scratch. That is happening right now, and the people who learn to build in this new world first will define the next twenty years. Superstars are being made this year, not in ten. 

HelloPrint is a €100M+ e-commerce company serving businesses across Europe and the US. We are rebuilding the entire company as AI-first: our platform, customer service, operations, and how we design, price, sell, and deliver. Every piece of technology we run is being rewritten as we speak. 

We are doing it with a small, senior, very fast AI development team working shoulder to shoulder with our business leads. Now we are opening a handful of seats for young builders who want to grow faster than any graduate scheme, bootcamp, or big-tech ladder could ever let them. 

We don't care if you are 16, 25 or 30, whether you are self-taught, hacking in high school, or finishing a degree at TU Delft or TU/e—we care about what you have built and how fast you solve hard problems. 

The HelloPrint AI Residency is how you start. It is a permanent role from day one: your first year is a structured residency where you rotate across our most important AI projects, build alongside the team and learn at full speed. After that, you keep growing - in the direction where you have the most impact. 

What you will actually do: 

You will not get a training plan, a sandbox project or six months of shadowing. From week one, you build real things that real customers and colleagues use, on the projects that matter most to the company. You sit next to the founders, next to the engineers who are rebuilding our platform, and next to the business leads who own the outcomes. You get a lot of freedom and real responsibility, plus honest, direct guidance and feedback from people who have built this before.

The kind of work you could be on in your first months: 

- Agentic Commerce : making HelloPrint discoverable and orderable through AI assistants, so a customer can order business cards from inside a chat. 

- AI Design Studio : letting customers create a print-ready design from a single sentence. 

- AI-first customer service : replacing classic ticketing with agents that resolve questions, check artwork and handle orders end to end. 

- Internal agent swarms : automating finance, purchasing, pricing and operations work that today still takes people hours. 

- Whatever you spot next : if you see something we should build, you pitch it, and if it is good, you build it. 

We work with almost every modern framework and model, and we change our tools the moment something better appears. You will ship, measure, throw away and ship again - every week. 

Who you are: 

- You are a builder before anything else . You have shipped things nobody asked you to build: an app, an agent, a bot, a tool your friends actually use, a side business, an open-source contribution, a weird experiment that taught you something. You probably have more GitHub commits, demos or deployed projects than most people twice your age. 

- You are extremely curious and extremely critical. You read the new model release the day it drops and try it that evening. You question every assumption, including ours, and you can explain why. You are never satisfied with "it works" — you want to know why it works, and how it could be ten times better. 

- You want to get better every single day, and you treat feedback as fuel rather than criticism. You take ownership: when something breaks, you fix it; when something is unclear, you go and find out. 

- You have a solid grasp of backend and software fundamentals (Python, APIs, databases) or the raw learning capacity to pick them up in weeks.

You will probably recognise yourself in most of this: 

- You build with AI every day: Claude, Cursor, Lovable, agents, APIs, whatever gets you there fastest. 

- You can show us concrete proof of work, not just tell us about it. 

- You move fast without being sloppy, and you care about the details the customer sees. 

- You are comfortable not knowing the answer, and you find it quickly. 

- You communicate clearly in English, in writing and out loud.

What we do not require: a degree, a minimum age, years of experience or a perfect CV. If you are still in school or university, we will make it work around that. 

What you get: 

The honest pitch: you will learn more here in one year than in five years almost anywhere else , because you will be building real systems for a real company that is reinventing itself, with the people who are leading that change. 

A contract from day one. The Residency is your first year at HelloPrint, not a trial period or an internship. 

- Direct access to the founders and to a senior AI development team who review your work and push you. 

- Ownership from day one : your name on projects that change how a €100M+ company runs. 

- The best tools, no budget debates : the newest models, coding agents and frameworks, as soon as they are worth using. 

- A growth path that follows your output, not your age : if you outgrow your role in six months, your role grows with you. 

- A fast, flat, no-politics team in Rotterdam, with a hands-on culture and a high bar. 

- Flexible set-up : full-time, or part-time alongside your studies. We care about what you deliver.

Salary and contract are tailored to your situation and your level, and we pay properly for real talent.

How to apply: 

Skip the cover letter. Show us what you have built.

Send us three things: 

- Your best project : a link to something you built: a live product, a repo, a demo video. Tell us in a few sentences what it does and what you would do differently now. 

- Something you think is broken : one thing about HelloPrint (our website, our ordering flow, anything) that you would rebuild with AI, and how you would do it. 

- A short intro : who you are and what you are obsessed with right now. Five sentences is plenty.

What happens next: 

- We read every application ourselves and reply within 5 days if you’re up to the next round 

- A 15-minute call with one of our builders or founders about your projects. 

- A Builders Day in our office: Together with other builders, you meet the team and if we have a click, you work on an assignment 

- A conversation with the founders, and a decision the same day.

We would rather hear from you too early than too late. If you are not sure you are ready, apply anyway; your work will answer that question for us. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

title: Account Executive  - DACH
description:
About the Role

We're building the sales engine for Tellent HR in the DACH market, and we're looking for an Account Executive to help us do it. Think of it as joining a startup inside a scale-up.

First and foremost, this is a hands-on selling role. You'll own the full sales cycle for Tellent HR (Manage and/or Grow), split roughly 80/20 between new business and expansion into our existing customer base. Inbound isn't going to be your main pipeline driver, so expect to spend around 50% of your time prospecting, against ambitious daily and weekly activity targets. Alongside that, you'll help us work out how we win in DACH: testing motions fast and doubling down on what drives revenue.

You'll work with a dedicated Product Marketing Manager and Customer Success Manager in the Tellent HR squad. CS capacity is limited, though, so you'll run deals independently, including demos and follow-through.

Your 12-Month Journey

- First 3 months: Learn Tellent HR, our ideal customers and the competitive landscape in DACH. Build your first pipeline through outbound, establish a consistent daily activity rhythm, and close your first deals.

- Within 6 months: Consistently hit your activity, pipeline and revenue targets, understand which sales motions work best in the DACH market, and feed insights back to Product Marketing and Product.

- After 1 year: Be the go-to expert on selling Tellent HR in DACH, with a repeatable, data-backed playbook that others can pick up.

What You'll Be Doing

- Own the full sales cycle, independently: Run 1–3 month, multi-stakeholder deals involving HR leaders, founders/CEOs and Finance, from first touch through to close and follow-through.

- Hunt for new pipeline (around 50% of your time): Prospect by phone, email and LinkedIn, consistently hit your daily and weekly activity targets, and maintain 3–4x pipeline coverage. Partner, CS and marketing leads are a bonus, not the plan.

- Drive expansion: Prospect into existing Tellent customers to cross-sell and upsell, e.g. Recruitee customers adding Tellent HR, or Manage customers adding Grow.

- Sell on value: Run consultative discovery and tailored demos, position on business outcomes, and handle objections, including against key competitors (with support from PMM).

- Manage deals with discipline: Use mutual action plans, keep HubSpot accurate (including SPICED), forecast reliably and disqualify early.

- Test and build, alongside selling: Experiment with sales motions, sequences and verticals, help build the playbook with our PMM, and bring customer and competitive insights from the DACH market back to Product and Marketing.

What You Bring

- Early-stage DNA: You've sold in a startup or early scale-up and built pipeline and processes where none existed. You know what it means to be an early sales hire.

- Proven hunter: A track record of self-generating pipeline through outbound and consistently hitting ambitious activity targets. You genuinely enjoy picking up the phone and creating opportunities from scratch.

- B2B SaaS sales experience: You've closed new business (ideally expansion too) as a fully autonomous AE in a startup or early scale-up, running 1–5 month, multi-stakeholder sales cycles. HR tech experience is a plus, not essential.

- Self-sufficient and resilient: You don't wait for leads, support teams or perfect processes. You bounce back from rejection and stay disciplined through the ups and downs of building something new.

- Consultative and data-driven: Strong discovery, demo and negotiation skills. You anchor on value before price and know your numbers (pipeline, conversion, win rate and cycle time).

- Languages: Fluent English and native or fluent German are required. You'll be responsible for engaging customers and building relationships across the DACH market.

This role probably isn't for you if you want a structured environment with large support teams and steady inbound, or you're more excited by GTM strategy than by picking up the phone every day.

How We Measure Success

- Closed-won revenue against target (primary KPI)

- Daily and weekly outbound activity targets (key leading indicator, especially early on)

- Self-generated pipeline and coverage

- Win rate, deal velocity and forecast accuracy

- Contributions to the playbook

What We Offer

- Compensation: €55000–€70000 gross annual base salary, plus commission .

- Ownership and impact: Real autonomy to shape the sales motion, playbook and market strategy for a growing product line.

- Hybrid working: Work from our canal-side Amsterdam office 2–3 days per week.

- International environment: Join a diverse and international team working across multiple markets.

- Learning & Development: €1,500 annual learning budget and 2 dedicated learning days.

- Pension & Wellness: Pension plan and wellness perks.

- Time Off: 28 paid holiday days, plus 2 additional days in 2026.

- Work from Anywhere: Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year.

- Commuting: Commuting and travel reimbursement.

- Home Office: €200 home office budget and a work-from-home allowance.

- Equipment: Apple MacBook and all the tools you need to succeed.

About Tellent

Tellent is a leading Talent Management Suite designed to empower HR & People teams across the entire employee journey. Our all-in-one platform combines an Applicant Tracking System ( Tellent Recruitee ), an intuitive HRIS ( Tellent HR ), and powerful Performance Management software ( Tellent Grow ).

With 250+ team members globally, 7,000+ customers in 100+ countries, and a growing ecosystem of 500+ partners, we help organizations attract, grow, and retain top talent — and we're just getting started.

AI in Our Recruitment Process

We use our internally developed AI tools to help streamline our recruitment process. However, technology never makes a decision. Every candidate is personally reviewed by our team. Your journey with us is guided by people, supported by tech. Curious about how it works? Read our AI Statement , check our Privacy Policy , or chat with us at 

If you require accommodations or support during the recruitment process, please let us know — we're happy to help.

About the Role

We're building the sales engine for Tellent HR in the French market, and we're looking for an Account Executive to help us do it. Think of it as joining a startup inside a scale-up.

First and foremost, this is a hands-on selling role. You'll own the full sales cycle for Tellent HR (Manage and/or Grow), split roughly 80/20 between new business and expansion into our existing customer base. Inbound isn't going to be your main pipeline driver, so expect to spend around 50% of your time prospecting, against ambitious daily and weekly activity targets. Alongside that, you'll help us work out how we win in France: testing motions fast and doubling down on what drives revenue.

You'll work with a dedicated Product Marketing Manager and Customer Success Manager in the Tellent HR squad. CS capacity is limited, though, so you'll run deals independently, including demos and follow-through.

- First 3 months: Learn Tellent HR, our ideal customers and the competitive landscape in France. Build your first pipeline through outbound, establish a consistent daily activity rhythm, and close your first deals.

- After 1 year: Be the go-to expert on selling Tellent HR in France, with a repeatable, data-backed playbook that others can pick up.

- Own the full sales cycle, independently: Run 1–3 month, multi-stakeholder deals involving HR leaders, founders/CEOs and Finance, from first touch through to close and follow-through.

This role probably isn't for you if you want a structured environment with large support teams and steady inbound, or you're more excited by GTM strategy than by picking up the phone every day.

title: Lead Java Software Engineer (v/m/x)
location: Capelle aan den IJssel, Zuid-Holland, Nederland
description:
Bouw mee aan de digitale toekomst van de openbare ruimte 

Bij Progresity ontwikkelen we software die gemeenten helpt om de openbare ruimte slimmer, veiliger en duurzamer te beheren. Onze applicatie BinnenBeter verbindt inwoners en gemeenten: via de BuitenBeter app kunnen inwoners eenvoudig meldingen doen van problemen in de openbare ruimte, van kapotte straatverlichting tot zwerfafval of een losliggende stoeptegel. Gemeenten ontvangen deze meldingen in BinnenBeter en kunnen ze efficiënt opvolgen, zodat elke melding leidt tot een zichtbare verbetering in de leefomgeving. Zo zorgen we samen voor schonere, veiligere en beter onderhouden steden voor miljoenen inwoners in Nederland.

We staan aan de vooravond van een belangrijke volgende stap. Niet alleen ontwikkelen we onze software verder, ook professionaliseren we de manier waarop we software bouwen. We willen groeien naar een moderne engineeringorganisatie waarin eigenaarschap, kwaliteit, automatisering en continu verbeteren centraal staan.

Daarom zoeken we een Lead Software Engineer (Java) die niet alleen technisch sterk is, maar ook energie krijgt van het verder brengen van een engineeringteam. Iemand die verder kijkt dan de code van vandaag, een duidelijke technische visie kan ontwikkelen en anderen weet mee te nemen in verandering. Die begrijpt dat goede software niet alleen draait om technologie, maar ook om samenwerking, vakmanschap en het maken van de juiste keuzes.

Jouw rol 

Als Lead Software Engineer (Java) combineer je hands-on software engineering met technisch leiderschap. Je werkt binnen een multidisciplinair productteam aan de verdere ontwikkeling van BinnenBeter en neemt het voortouw in de technische richting en professionalisering van Engineering.

Je bent eigenaar van de technische visie en architectuur van het product. Je bepaalt samen met je collega's hoe we onze software toekomstbestendig houden en vertaalt technische ambities naar concrete verbeteringen. Daarbij kijk je verder dan nieuwe functionaliteiten: ook onderhoudbaarheid, schaalbaarheid, security, betrouwbaarheid en technische schuld krijgen structureel aandacht.

Tegelijkertijd ben je een belangrijke kartrekker in het verbeteren van onze manier van werken. Hoe kunnen we sneller en betrouwbaarder releasen? Hoe maken we geautomatiseerd testen en CI/CD vanzelfsprekend? Hoe zorgen we dat engineers verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor hun software, ook nadat deze in productie staat?

Je hoeft deze uitdagingen niet alleen op te lossen. Je coacht Software Engineers, stimuleert eigenaarschap en zorgt dat technische kennis en verantwoordelijkheden niet bij één persoon blijven liggen.

Je gaat onder andere aan de slag met:

- Het ontwikkelen, uitdragen en bewaken van de technische visie en softwarearchitectuur van BinnenBeter.

- Het ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van robuuste, onderhoudbare en schaalbare software met Java en Spring Boot.

- Het richting geven aan belangrijke technische keuzes en het ontwikkelen en borgen van engineeringstandaarden en architectuurprincipes.

- Het vertalen van relevante wet- en regelgeving en beveiligingseisen naar concrete technische richtlijnen.

- Het verbeteren van onze engineeringpraktijken, waaronder CI/CD, testautomatisering, observability en DevOps.

- Het inzichtelijk maken en structureel aanpakken van technische schuld, kwetsbaarheden en andere technische risico's.

- Het ontwikkelen en realiseren van een technische verbeteragenda, samen met het engineeringteam.

- Het coachen van Software Engineers en stimuleren van zelfstandigheid, kennisdeling en technisch eigenaarschap.

- Het versterken van de samenwerking tussen Engineering, Product, UX, Quality en Cloud/Platform.

- Het onderzoeken van nieuwe technologieën en werkwijzen, waaronder AI, die onze software of manier van ontwikkelen daadwerkelijk beter maken.

Wat neem je mee? 

We zoeken een ervaren Software Engineer die inhoudelijk sterk is, maar ook begrijpt dat technisch leiderschap meer vraagt dan het maken van goede technische keuzes.

Je kunt complexe vraagstukken analyseren en een duidelijke richting bepalen. Tegelijkertijd weet je anderen daarin mee te nemen, sta je open voor andere perspectieven en haal je voldoening uit het ontwikkelen van collega's.

Wat we belangrijk vinden: 

- Ruime ervaring met Java en Spring Boot en een sterke achtergrond in professionele software engineering.

- Ervaring met softwarearchitectuur, REST API's en het ontwerpen van onderhoudbare en schaalbare applicaties.

- Je kunt complexe technische vraagstukken doorgronden, alternatieven afwegen en onderbouwde technische keuzes maken.

- Je hebt ervaring met het ontwikkelen of verbeteren van technische standaarden, architectuurprincipes en engineeringpraktijken.

- Je hebt kennis van moderne softwareontwikkeling, waaronder CI/CD, geautomatiseerd testen, security en observability.

- Je hebt ervaring met het begeleiden of coachen van andere Software Engineers en vindt het leuk om collega's technisch verder te helpen.

- Je communiceert helder, kunt technische onderwerpen begrijpelijk uitleggen en weet verschillende disciplines met elkaar te verbinden.

- Je neemt initiatief, durft verantwoordelijkheid te nemen en weet ideeën om te zetten in concrete verbeteringen.

- Je bent pragmatisch en kunt een goede balans vinden tussen technische kwaliteit, ontwikkelsnelheid en klantwaarde.

- Je bent beschikbaar voor 32, 36 of 40 uur per week.

Mooi meegenomen, maar geen vereiste: 

- Ervaring met Angular en TypeScript.

- Ervaring met WildFly, Azure, Docker, Kubernetes of vergelijkbare technologieën.

- Ervaring met het begeleiden van technische veranderingen of het professionaliseren van een engineeringteam.

- Ervaring met cloud-native architecturen, DevOps en het beheren van software in productie.

Je hoeft niet eerder de functietitel Lead Software Engineer te hebben gehad. Misschien ben je nu Senior Software Engineer of Software Architect en merk je dat je steeds vaker technische richting geeft, collega's begeleidt en verbeteringen initieert. Als je klaar bent om daarin een volgende stap te zetten, gaan we graag met je in gesprek.

Dan bieden wij jou 

- Een salaris tussen €4.500,- en €6.690,- bruto per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur), afhankelijk van jouw ervaring.

- Een rol waarin je daadwerkelijk invloed hebt op de technische richting van onze software en de ontwikkeling van Engineering.

- Veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief, technische verbeteringen en het toepassen van nieuwe technologieën.

- Hybride werken met flexibele werktijden en een modern kantoor in Capelle aan den IJssel.

- Werken in een team waar jouw ideeën daadwerkelijk worden gehoord.

- 8% vakantiegeld.

- 25 vakantiedagen met de mogelijkheid om 5 extra dagen bij te kopen.

- Laptop van de zaak.

- Goede pensioenregeling en collectieve bonus.

- Een jaarcontract met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband.

- Een rol waarin jouw werk iedere dag maatschappelijke impact heeft.

Over Progresity 

Progresity is onderdeel van de Conxillium Group. Samen ontwikkelen we slimme software voor gemeenten. Onze producten ondersteunen gemeenten bij het beheren van de openbare ruimte: van bomen en groenvoorzieningen tot wegen, verlichting en meldingen van inwoners.

We bevinden ons in een interessante fase. We groeien van een traditionele softwareorganisatie naar productgerichte teams waarin eigenaarschap, samenwerking en continu verbeteren centraal staan. Dat betekent dat developers bij ons niet alleen meedenken over hoe we software bouwen, maar ook over waarom we iets bouwen en welke waarde dat oplevert voor onze gebruikers.

Je komt terecht in een hecht team waarin vakmanschap, nieuwsgierigheid en elkaar helpen belangrijker zijn dan hiërarchie. We geloven dat de beste ideeën ontstaan wanneer mensen verantwoordelijkheid krijgen en samen blijven leren.

Lees meer over onze organisatie op: www.progresity.com .

Sollicitatieproces 

Ons sollicitatieproces bestaat meestal uit drie gesprekken. We vinden het belangrijk dat we elkaar goed leren kennen. Naast jouw technische kennis zijn we vooral benieuwd hoe jij samenwerkt, hoe je naar softwareontwikkeling kijkt en hoe jij jezelf én een team verder helpt groeien.

Enthousiast? 

Wil jij bijdragen aan slimmere, veiligere en duurzamere software voor gemeenten én meebouwen aan de volgende stap van onze engineeringorganisatie? Reageer dan via de sollicitatiebutton of neem contact op met onze recruiter Steven Kruis via 06 57 43 92 61 of

title: Agent Security Engineer
description:
Belmont Lavan is hiring an Agent Security Engineer to secure autonomous AI agents before and after they reach production. Agents now call tools, hold credentials and act on live systems, so they need the controls we already expect for people and services: identity, least-privilege access, monitoring and testing.

You will sit between AI engineering and security. You will design the guardrails, attack the systems yourself, and build the governance controls that let the business deploy agents with confidence.

Requirements 

- 5+ years in security engineering (AppSec, cloud security, IAM or offensive security), with at least 1 year securing LLM or agent-based systems
- Hands-on knowledge of LLM attack techniques: prompt injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration via tools, RAG poisoning
- Experience designing identity and access controls: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, token exchange, workload identity, secrets management
- Working knowledge of agent frameworks and protocols such as LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI or Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Strong coding skills in Python, plus one of Go, TypeScript or Rust
- Cloud security on AWS, Azure or GCP, including logging, detection and policy-as-code (e.g. OPA / Cedar)
- Ability to explain AI risk clearly to engineers, risk teams and executives

title: Head of Product Experience
description:
At Vio , we believe booking accommodation should feel fair and effortless, never overwhelming or unclear.

As one of the world's fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of travelers find and book the right stay at the right price. They can book with us directly, compare offers across 100+ booking sites, or book through partners who offer our experience under their own brand.

Our goal is to help travelers book like an insider. That means cutting through the noise and complexity of hotel booking and surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays, booked with confidence.

With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology that travelers can trust.

🔍 Who we're looking for 

We're looking for a senior design leader to own Vio's whole user experience: Product Design, UX Research and Content Design, and the product outcomes they serve. You'll lead a team of around ten across design, research and content. This is a chance to build a function, not inherit one.

You'll report to our Head of Product and sit in domain leadership alongside product, engineering and commercial leaders, shaping strategy from the start. Vio runs two businesses on one platform: our consumer product, and white-label and API products for partners. Your job is to make the experience across both recognisably world-class, and to build a team that can sustain it.

☑️ What you'll do 

- Set the UX vision for Vio's next chapter, and bring product, engineering and commercial partners along with it.

- Own user-facing outcomes with your peers, and make design's contribution measurable.

- Lead Product Design, UX Research and Content Design, and design the org that brings them together in your first 90 days.

- Set and hold the craft bar: run critique and product reviews, and make journeys consistent across our products and brands.

- Work with Product and Engineering on how we ship, not only what we ship: bring design into problem framing early, and raise the quality of what reaches our users.

- Build a team people want to join and stay in: clear ownership, air cover, real growth paths, and recognition for great work.

- Stay close to the work, with ring-fenced time on north-star concepts and cross-product journeys.

- Make AI part of how design, research and content work.

- Give design a stronger voice inside Vio and a visible presence outside it.

🔎 Who you are 

- You've led a multi-discipline UX organisation (design and design systems, research, content) at scale, including leaders of leaders, with real depth across all three, including research.

- You frame the problem before the solution, make trade-offs between user and commercial needs, and can show the outcomes and metrics you've moved with Product.

- You're a credible peer to senior product, engineering and business leaders, and you influence beyond design.

- You've designed B2B2C products, where partners offer the product to their own customers and judge it as well as end users.

- Your own craft holds up at the highest level: you lead critique, set the quality bar in the details, and articulate a vision that others rally behind.

- You build teams that grow, and you hire people stronger than yourself.

- You use AI in your own practice and know how to scale it across a team.

Nice to have: travel, marketplace or OTA experience; multi-brand or white-label design systems; a visible external profile through talks, writing or case studies. 

❓ Why join us now? 

- You'll build Vio's design function and shape its UX from a seat in domain leadership, at a pivotal moment for the company.

- We're one of the fastest-growing accommodation booking platforms in the world today, having grown our bookings 30x between 2017 and 2025, and catering to the needs of millions of travelers each year.

- In 2026, we underwent a company-wide rebrand and launched our first StoryTelling marketing campaign in the UK, establishing Vio as a consumer-facing, creative brand.

- Our mobile apps ( iOS and Android ) have reached 5 million installs with strong customer reviews.

- We reward our employees for the value they create by granting Stock Appreciation Rights to all employees.

➕ What we offer 

- Plenty of chances to learn and grow within an open, diverse culture that promotes knowledge sharing, trust, and transparency.

- A great compensation package, perks, and benefits - including significant stock appreciation rights.

- Flexible time off, with as many holidays as you need, and a chance to work remotely.

- You'll be part of an international team in one of the best office locations in Amsterdam.

- We value good food and offer catered lunches from various cuisines, great coffee, and the occasional barbecue in our garden.

- We enjoy getting together to celebrate our wins, with company events in Amsterdam and abroad.

- A budget for your home office.

title: Architecture Internship Dutch | March 2027 (2)
description:
Geef je carrière een vliegende start 

MVRDV is een wereldwijd gerenommeerd architectuur- en stedenbouwkundig bureau met het hoofdkantoor in Rotterdam en kantoren in Shanghai, Parijs, Berlijn en New York. MVRDV werd in 1993 opgericht door Winy Maas, Jacob van Rijs en Nathalie de Vries en zet zich in voor het ontwerpen van innovatieve, maatschappelijk verantwoorde en duurzame architectuur die de toekomst vormgeeft. 

Als stagiair bij MVRDV maak je deel uit van een energiek, internationaal team van meer dan 200 professionals uit ruim 40 verschillende landen. Je doet praktijkervaring op in baanbrekende projecten, werkt samen met toonaangevende architecten en verlegt de grenzen van ontwerp en innovatie. Ben jij gepassioneerd over architectuur en wil je leren in een dynamische en creatieve omgeving? Dan horen we graag van je. 

Let op: We verzoeken recruitmentbureaus vriendelijk om geen ongevraagde kandidaten of profielen voor deze vacature aan te leveren. Wij verzorgen het wervingsproces intern en accepteren geen voorwaarden of vergoedingen met betrekking tot ongevraagde doorverwijzingen. 

Sollicitatieprocedure 

- Je kunt je sollicitatie indienen vanaf nu tot en met 16 november 2026 . 

- De gesprekken vinden plaats tussen 23 november en 11 december 2026 . 

- Succesvolle kandidaten starten op 1 maart 2027 . 

Belangrijk: Om in aanmerking te komen voor deze stage moet je gedurende de volledige stageperiode, van 1 maart 2027 tot en met 31 augustus 2027 , ingeschreven blijven staan aan een daarvoor in aanmerking komende opleiding aan een universiteit of hogeschool. 

Over het Design Collective 

Het Design Collective van MVRDV is verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen van innovatieve en duurzame gebouwen en constructies. We werken aan een breed scala aan projecten, van kleinschalige woningbouw tot grootschalige commerciële en culturele complexen. Bekijk enkele voorbeelden van onze projecten op: https://www.mvrdv.com/projects. 

Het Design Collective richt zich op projecten in de volgende regio’s: 

- Nederland 

- Azië 

- DACH-regio 

- Franstalige landen 

- Noord-Amerika 

- Centraal- en Oost-Europa 

- Taiwan 

- Midden-Oosten 

Over de functie 

Als Architectuurstagiair bij MVRDV kom je terecht in een dynamische omgeving waar gedurfde ideeën en snel schakelen dagelijks centraal staan. Je wordt begeleid door internationaal vooraanstaande ontwerpers bij projecten en prijsvragen en levert een bijdrage aan ambitieuze concepten, gedetailleerde tekeningen en indrukwekkende visualisaties. 

Afhankelijk van jouw profiel en ervaring word je gekoppeld aan specifieke projecten, regio’s en/of projecttypen. 

Dit is een uitstekende kans om je vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen, je creativiteit uit te dagen en een realistisch beeld te krijgen van het werken aan de voorhoede van de architectuur.

- Assisteren bij de ontwikkeling van concepten en ontwerpvoorstellen. 

- Maken van tekeningen, diagrammen en 3D-modellen. 

- Ontwikkelen van visualisaties en presentatiemateriaal voor prijsvragen en opdrachtgevers. 

- Deelnemen aan teamoverleggen en ontwerpbesprekingen. 

- Onderzoek doen naar materialen, locatieomstandigheden en architectonische referenties. 

Wat bieden wij?

Leren van marktleiders

Word onderdeel van een wereldwijd, ambitieus en optimistisch team dat werkt aan architectonische en stedenbouwkundige vraagstukken over de hele wereld. Je werkt samen met professionals uit verschillende disciplines, van ontwerp tot business support. 

Stagevergoeding 

Je ontvangt een aantrekkelijke stagevergoeding van €1.100 per maand , plus een vergoeding voor je woon-werkverkeer (via een NS-Business Card of kilometervergoeding).

Geniet van betaalbare vegetarische lunches op kantoor (€4,30 per dag), een ruime bijdrage aan je Urban Sports Club-abonnement en toegang tot OpenUp , ons platform voor mentaal welzijn. 

Een inspirerende werkplek

Werk vanuit ons kantoor in de levendige Rotterdamse wijk Blaak , op loopafstand van station Rotterdam Blaak. Een inspirerende omgeving in het hart van de stad.

Meer specifiek zoeken wij studenten met: 

- Sterke ontwerp- en CAD-vaardigheden. 

- Goede beheersing van Adobe Suite en sterke 2D- en 3D-visualisatievaardigheden (vermeld in je sollicitatie duidelijk je ervaring met de verschillende softwareprogramma’s). 

- Het vermogen om goed samen te werken in internationale teams. 

- Uitstekende mondelinge en schriftelijke beheersing van de Engelse taal ; aanvullende talen zijn een pré. 

- Werkgerechtigdheid in Nederland (bijvoorbeeld door EU-burgerschap, een Nederlandse verblijfsvergunning of een Working Holiday-visum). Indien van toepassing kan MVRDV ondersteuning bieden bij de visumaanvraag voor niet-EU-burgers. Dit is afhankelijk van het voldoen aan alle vereisten van de Nederlandse Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst (IND). Zorg er daarom voor dat je de juiste gegevens invult in je sollicitatie. 

- Gedurende de volledige stageperiode ingeschreven staan als student (een bewijs van inschrijving is vereist). 

Sluit je bij ons aan en doe waardevolle praktijkervaring op in een dynamische en collaboratieve werkomgeving, waar jouw ideeën ertoe doen en jouw ontwikkeling wordt gestimuleerd, of je nu werkzaam bent in design, communicatie, HR, finance of een andere discipline. 

Wij kijken ernaar uit je in ons team te verwelkomen!

description:
About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

#LI-IV1 

The role 

The Service Desk IT Operations Lead is the senior individual contributor on the Service Desk path and the senior technical escalation point for Service Desk across EMEA and APAC . The role owns and improves Service Desk processes, runbooks, escalation paths, the employee hardware lifecycle and new-hire IT onboarding, administers Service Desk tooling on behalf of its owners, and leads improvement initiatives and cross-functional projects. It acts as the bridge between the Service Desk and Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications and Security, and leads through expertise, judgment and influence rather than formal authority. It carries no line-management responsibility.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- 
Serve as the final technical escalation point within Service Desk for high-severity, high-complexity and business-critical issues, before engagement of Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Security or vendors; coordinate major-incident response, communication and post-incident follow-through with the relevant teams.

- 
Act as consultation point for L1/L2 on complex or unusual cases: advise on troubleshooting approach, ownership, escalation path and resolution before issues are escalated.

- 
Act as subject matter expert for the end-user computing environment: endpoints (Windows, macOS), mobile devices, identity and access (Entra ID / Active Directory, SSO , MFA ), Microsoft 365, MDM , collaboration tools and meeting-room technology.

- 
Administer and configure Service Desk tooling (e.g. Jira Service Management workflows and automation, device enrolment and MDM policy, hardware asset management tooling) as agreed with the tool and platform owners, and propose and implement improvements, including request workflows and automations used by adjacent functions. Ownership of the tools and platforms sits with IT leadership and platform owners.

- 
Administer selected corporate IT systems and services according to operational requirements, including access and permissions management, service configuration and automation.

- 
Maintain and improve Service Desk procedures, runbooks, escalation paths and knowledge base; propose technical standards for approval by Service Desk management and maintain them once approved; advise on operational priorities.

- 
Contribute to creating and updating documentation: runbooks, process documents, technical standards and knowledge-base articles, setting the standard for documentation quality across the team.

- 
Analyze ticket, escalation and SLA data to identify systemic issues and contribute to SLA reporting; lead root-cause analysis and problem management; design process, tooling and automation changes that improve first-time resolution and reduce escalation volume.

- 
Assess proposed solutions and operational changes for supportability and user impact; advise management and partner teams on the support implications of technology decisions.

- 
Provide organizational context on existing and legacy IT processes, systems, decisions and ownership structures; apply it when evaluating current processes, and improve legacy practices where appropriate.

- 
Identify gaps or ambiguities in operational ownership and work with the relevant stakeholders to establish practical solutions.

- 
Own and improve employee-lifecycle processes, including hardware provisioning and, with Onboarding and People teams, new-hire IT onboarding across EMEA and APAC .

- 
Recommend standards for company-provided laptops, peripherals and other end-user equipment, balancing business need, supportability, lifecycle and market availability; maintain the approved standards.

- 
Own employee hardware lifecycle processes, provisioning, replacement, reuse, return, disposal and employee resale, and provide demand forecasts and regional requirements (including Bill & Hold) to IT Supply Chain and Procurement; recommend routine purchases against agreed standards, approving only within a documented delegated spend limit.

- 
Lead and continuously improve equipment reuse and employee resale, including TechShop.

- 
Contribute to forecasting and budget planning for employee technology and Service Desk requirements.

- 
Support Service Desk contracts, renewals and licensing; maintain working relationships with hardware and Service Desk vendors.

- 
Lead Service Desk projects, system migrations, new technology rollouts, process optimization, and contribute Service Desk expertise to company initiatives such as regional expansion, office launches, organizational changes and onboarding improvements, working with Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Security, HR/People, Onboarding, Recruiting, Procurement, Workplace/Facilities and the AV /Builds team.

- 
Advise partner functions on Service Desk capabilities, procedures, requirements and dependencies, and work with them to define and improve shared operational processes (e.g. joiner/mover/leaver with People, office launches with Workplace).

- 
Act as technical interviewer in Service Desk recruitment, providing structured feedback and hiring recommendations to management, and technical input to role requirements.

- 
Deliver technical onboarding for new team members and mentor L1 and L2 through joint troubleshooting, coaching and knowledge transfer, documenting approaches to reduce reliance on individual knowledge.

- 
Stay hands-on: support the IT Bar, queue and events alongside L1/L2 when needed, and lead by example on ticket quality and communication.

- 
Provide operational evidence for audits and compliance (including equipment lifecycle and offboarding); follow security, access-governance and procurement requirements; escalate material concerns to the appropriate owner.

We expect you to have: 

- 
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology or related field, or equivalent experience.

- 
5+ years of IT support or service desk experience with demonstrated progression in responsibility.

- 
Advanced technical certifications (Microsoft 365, Azure, ITIL Intermediate, Security+, etc.) strongly preferred.

- 
Deep knowledge of enterprise IT systems, networks, and security practices.

- 
Strong leadership, coaching, and collaboration skills.

- 
Proven ability to manage high-priority incidents and lead cross-functional troubleshooting efforts.

Related Competencies 

- 
Knowledge & Skills 

- 
Recognised expert in end-user computing and support operations, with breadth across endpoints, identity, collaboration, device management and security touch points.

Diagnoses ambiguous, cross-platform issues; experienced in root-cause analysis and process optimisation.

Translates complex issues into clear guidance for technical and non-technical audiences.

- 
Autonomy 

- 
Operates with a high degree of independence and trusted judgment.

Takes the most sensitive escalations from intake to follow-up.

Independently identifies improvements and drives them to completion; proactively pitches projects within the Service Desk domain.

Advises management and partner teams on the support implications of technology decisions. Significant spend, strategic or organisational changes, and decisions outside delegated authority are aligned with management.

- 
Complexity 

- 
Handles the most complex technical and operational problems in the support function: multiple systems, conflicting signals, incomplete data, elevated business risk.

Leads escalations, often coordinating multiple IT functions.

Designs and improves workflows and procedures where no precedent exists.

- 
Impact 

- 
Broad impact on service reliability, SLA performance, support maturity and user experience across EMEA and APAC .

Reduces downtime, repeat incidents and escalation volume.

Shapes employee technology from onboarding through equipment return; ensures knowledge transfer and team readiness.

- 
People / Leadership

Leads through expertise, coordination and example, not formal authority.

Escalation point and mentor for L1 and L2; shapes team capability over time. Technical interviewer.

No line management: hiring decisions, performance, compensation and other people-management accountabilities sit with Service Desk management.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
For this role, we will only consider candidates who are currently based in the Netherlands. 

About SkinVision 

Skin cancer is highly treatable when caught early, but limited access to specialist care and long wait times delay diagnosis, increasing the risk of late-stage cases and driving up treatment costs. SkinVision, founded in Amsterdam in 2012, exists to close that gap. Our proprietary AI — certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU regulation, with over 90% sensitivity and 89% specificity — has already helped nearly 3 million people worldwide detect early signs of skin cancer. Today, SkinVision has a database of more than 6 million skin spot assessments and can reach 20 million people through insurer partnerships. High-risk cases are reviewed by a team of dermatologists, who support users in taking the right next step — from urgent care to a specialist referral. We are extending this further, connecting users faster to the specialist care they need. We're a focused, international team, active globally, united by one goal: making early detection accessible to everyone, everywhere. If you join us, you're not just building a product — you're helping close the gap between a person noticing something and getting the care they need. 

DevOps at SkinVision 

As a DevOps Engineer at SkinVision, you will play a key role in building, scaling, and securing the infrastructure that powers our AI-driven health platform. You’ll design and maintain our cloud-based systems in AWS, implement CI/CD pipelines, enhance observability using Datadog, and drive operational excellence through automation and monitoring. 

Your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of a medical-grade system that serves users globally. You’ll collaborate closely with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure smooth delivery, rapid deployments, and resilient operations — ultimately enabling us to deliver life-saving technology with confidence. 

Beyond hands-on expertise with AWS and modern DevOps tooling, we’re looking for someone who thinks architecturally. You’ll get to know our current setup, form your own view of how it should evolve, and help define a target vision for our infrastructure, then drive its implementation. Day-to-day operational work is part of the role, but we value someone who thinks before building and takes ownership of where our infrastructure goes next. 

What you will do 

Cloud Infrastructure & Automation 

- Design, build, and manage AWS-based infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. 

- Implement and manage infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation. 

- Automate environment provisioning, configuration, and deployments using CI/CD pipelines. 

- Ensure system resilience, security, and performance through automated monitoring and alerting. 

CI/CD & Deployment 

- Design and optimize CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, reliable, and safe deployments across environments. 

- Manage deployment workflows using Argo CD and Kubernetes. 

- Collaborate with developers and ML engineers to streamline build, test, and release processes. 

- Integrate automated testing, rollback strategies, and version control into the deployment lifecycle. 

Observability & Monitoring 

- Build a comprehensive observability stack using Datadog for metrics, logs, traces, and alerts. 

- Define service-level objectives (SLOs), service-level indicators (SLIs), and dashboards for system performance. 

- Proactively detect and resolve performance bottlenecks, capacity issues, and reliability risks. 

- Create automated health checks and ensure visibility across production systems. 

Security & Compliance 

- Implement security best practices for AWS, containers, and CI/CD pipelines. 

- Manage identity, access, and secret handling (IAM, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store). 

- Ensure compliance with medical device standards and data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA). 

- Partner with the Information Security Officer to embed security controls across infrastructure and deployments. 

Reliability & Incident Management 

- Lead incident response and root cause analysis for infrastructure or deployment-related issues. 

- Establish SLAs and operational runbooks for production environments. 

- Continuously improve system reliability through chaos testing, redundancy, and fault tolerance. 

- Mentor engineers on DevOps principles, observability practices, and infrastructure automation. 

Infrastructure Strategy & Architecture 

- Assess the current infrastructure and deployment setup, and form a well-reasoned view of how it should evolve. 

- Define and maintain a target architecture for our cloud platform, balancing reliability, scalability, security, and cost. 

- Translate the target vision into a practical roadmap and drive its implementation incrementally, alongside day-to-day operations. 

- Document and communicate architectural decisions, aligning with engineering and leadership on technical direction. 

Essential skills 

- Minimum of 6 years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Infrastructure roles. 

- Strong expertise with AWS services (EC2, ECS/EKS, S3, RDS, CloudWatch, Lambda, etc.). 

- Expert in Kubernetes and Argo CD, deploying and managing production-grade custom Helm charts with secure, automated GitOps workflows in EKS 

- Advanced knowledge of CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar). 

- Proficiency in Datadog for observability, monitoring, and alerting. 

- Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, Bash, or Go. 

- Experience managing infrastructure with Terraform, CloudFormation, or Ansible. 

- Familiarity with networking fundamentals, load balancing, and API gateway configuration. 

- Excellent problem-solving and incident management skills. 

Desirable skills 

- Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, MedTech, or FinTech. 

- Familiarity with multi-environment architecture (staging, pre-prod, production) and blue-green deployments. 

- Exposure to event-driven systems, message queues, and data streaming (Kafka, SNS/SQS). 

- Understanding of Zero Trust networking and cloud security best practices. 

- Experience in cost optimization and performance tuning in AWS. 

Qualifications 

- A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 

- Certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), or Terraform Associate are a plus. 

What we offer 

- A competitive salary, additional benefits, and a hybrid working policy 

- A vibrant, dynamic, and rapidly growing scale-up in Amsterdam 

- An enthusiastic, professional, and international team 

- Regular team events, including off-sites and fun activities 

- Unlimited skin checks for you

You help evolve a mature monolithic codebase into a more modular, testable and future-proof architecture. By modernising the foundation of the product, you directly enable better user experiences, faster iteration and higher overall product quality. 

What you'll do 

Drive technical excellence 

- Design and deliver high-quality, scalable solutions for complex features and system components

Build for reliability and scale

Core technical expertise

title: wo-stage onderzoek milieukosten m.b.v. bestaande afval- en emissiestatistieken
description:
wo- afstudeerstage/praktijkstage, vanaf februari 2027 

Ben jij die nieuwsgierige onderzoeker die energie krijgt van data, duurzaamheid en nieuwe inzichten?
Wil jij een inhoudelijke bijdrage leveren aan de statistieken van het CBS? 

Dit is jouw uitdaging 

Het kabinet wil dat Nederland in 2050 volledig circulair is. Om te kunnen volgen of we die doelstelling halen, is betrouwbare informatie nodig over onder andere afval en emissies naar water. Het CBS verzamelt en publiceert deze gegevens voor bedrijven. Daarbij maken we vooral gebruik van gegevens uit het elektronisch Milieujaarverslag (e-MJV), aangevuld met enquêtes. 

Naast de hoeveelheid afval en wateremissies brengen we ook de milieukosten van bedrijven in kaart, bijvoorbeeld de kosten voor afvalverwerking en voor het lozen van afvalwater. Hiervoor wordt nu een aparte enquête gebruikt. Maar is dat eigenlijk wel nodig? 

Tijdens je stage onderzoek je of we de milieukosten voor afval en wateremissies kunnen berekenen met gegevens die al beschikbaar zijn. Je combineert bijvoorbeeld gegevens over de hoeveelheid afval en geloosd water met bestaande indicatoren, zoals gemiddelde kosten per ton afval en sectorspecifieke kosten per kubieke meter geloosd water. 

Je gaat onder andere: 

- bestaande data en indicatoren analyseren en beoordelen op bruikbaarheid; 

- onderzoeken welke methode het meest geschikt is om de milieukosten te schatten; 

- een berekening of model ontwikkelen waarmee de kosten kunnen worden afgeleid; 

- de uitkomsten vergelijken met de beschikbare gegevens uit de huidige enquête; 

- onderzoeken hoe betrouwbaar en bruikbaar de schattingen zijn; 

- je bevindingen vertalen naar een concreet advies voor het CBS. 

Met jouw onderzoek willen we bepalen of we meer uit bestaande data kunnen halen en minder hoeven uit te vragen bij bedrijven. Als blijkt dat de milieukosten betrouwbaar kunnen worden berekend, kunnen de uitkomsten bovendien worden gebruikt om de bestaande afval- en waterstatistieken te controleren. 

In het meest gunstige scenario kan de aparte enquête naar milieukosten gedeeltelijk of helemaal vervallen. Dat betekent minder administratieve lasten voor bedrijven, efficiënter gebruik van beschikbare data en mogelijk betrouwbaardere statistieken. 

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Den Haag 

We verwelkomen je binnen de sector Leefomgeving bij team Milieu. Met 20 gedreven professionals werken we aan milieu gerelateerde statistieken en doen we onderzoek naar actuele thema’s zoals klimaat(verandering) en circulaire economie. We werken nauw samen met andere teams binnen het CBS. 

We werken hard aan het continu verbeteren van onze statistieken en de cijfers beschikbaar te stellen voor het publiek. Voorbeelden van recente publicaties uit ons team zijn: 

- Bedrijven investeerden in 2024 minder in milieu | CBS 

- Bijna 2 procent meer bedrijfs- en industrieafval in 2021 | CBS 

- Milieukosten en -investeringen van bedrijven | CBS 

Dit breng jij mee 

Je volgt een wo-opleiding milieukunde, economie, technische bestuurskunde, data science of een aanverwante opleiding. 

- Je hebt affiniteit met het onderwerp circulaire economie. 

- Je bent analytisch sterk en kunt complexe vraagstukken gestructureerd onderzoeken en vertalen naar heldere inzichten. 

- Je kunt goed programmeren in R. 

- Je bent sociaal en communicatief vaardig en kunt je ideeën en bevindingen helder overbrengen aan verschillende gesprekspartners. 

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk. 

Dit kun je van ons verwachten 

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je: 

- jouw competenties in kwantitatieve data-analyse versterkt door gebruik te maken van milieustatistieken en economische databronnen; 

- jouw onderzoeksvaardigheden aanscherpt op het gebied van de circulaire economie en levenscyclusanalyse; 

- jouw programmeervaardigheden in R verder ontwikkelt; 

- ervaring opdoet met het interpreteren van verschillende datasets om betrouwbare profielen op te stellen. 

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800 bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week). 

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken. 

Dit zijn onze voorwaarden 

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken. 
Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking.

title: Strategy & Operations Lead, Data & Intelligence
description:
GRESB is the global sustainability intelligence standard for real assets. For over 15 years, real estate and infrastructure managers have reported to us, building a dataset of 150,000+ assets across more than 2,000 portfolios. Together with Asset Impact, which tracks emissions for over 300,000 physical assets and 77,000 companies, we’re turning that data into decision-grade intelligence for investors, lenders, index providers and regulators.

We’re building a new Client & Data Intelligence organization to showcase the value of the data to investors and develop new use cases within the ecosystem. It brings sales, product and data teams together under one leader, the Chief Client & Data Intelligence Officer. This role is the person who makes that organization run. The role is based out of Amsterdam.

The Role 

You’ll work directly with the Chief Client & Data Intelligence Officer as the strategist and operator at the center of a newly formed team. Your job is to keep decisions moving, teams connected and priority work getting finished, so the leadership team can focus on clients and growth.

It’s a role for someone who can shape a problem and then see it through. One week you might be building the business case for a new data product; the next you’re tightening the sales pipeline, preparing a board update and unblocking a delivery issue between product and engineering. You’ll move between sales enablement, product and data operations, and you’ll be trusted to run several projects at once without dropping any of them.

You’ll see the whole business, from client conversations to product decisions to the CEO’s agenda, and you’ll have influence over how a new organization works.

What you will do 

Strategy and priority projects 

- Lead the organization’s highest-priority initiatives end to end, for example pricing, our investor program, entry into new markets and maturing the data strategy
- Frame the problem, build the analysis, align stakeholders and drive the work through to a decision and implementation
- Bring a recommendation, not just options
Operating rhythm and decision-making 

- Run the team’s operating cadence: weekly deal desk, fortnightly product council and monthly business review
- Own the decision log, so it’s always clear what was decided, by whom and what happens next
- Spot blockers between sales, product and data teams early and clear them
Commercial operations and sales enablement 

- Own pricing and support deal structuring with the sales team
- Keep pipeline and ARR reporting accurate and trusted, with one view across GRESB
- Work with sales and product to make sure the team has what it needs to showcase the value of the data products
Reporting and communication 

- Build and run the monthly CEO dashboard and KPI reporting
- Prepare senior leadership, board and client materials that are clear, concise and decision-ready
- Act as the Chief Client & Data Intelligence Officer’s point of contact when they’re away

What success looks like 

In your first six months

- The operating rhythm is running and people rely on it
- The decision log is live and used
- There’s one trusted ARR view across GRESB data products
By the end of your first year

- At least two priority projects have been taken from problem to implemented decision
- Leadership and board reporting runs on a predictable monthly cycle with little rework
- Sales, product and data teams describe fewer handoff issues, and escalations get resolved faster
Requirements 

- Around 6–10 years of experience
- A grounding in top-tier management consulting or Big Four advisory, in strategy, sustainability, data or technology
- Ideally, spent time at a sustainability data, ESG ratings, real asset or financial data business
- Strong business acumen and ability to work well in a cross-functional, global environment.
- Experience implementing AI or advanced analytics solutions within a commercial or sales environment.
- Proficiency in CRM, data analytics, and visualization tools.
- A working understanding of how data products are packaged, priced and sold

How you work 

- You think in structure: you can break down an ambiguous problem, find what matters and build a clear path forward
- You finish things. You run several projects at once and see each one through to the end
- You’re organized, detail-oriented and work well in systems
- You write and present clearly, whether it’s a one-page update or a board deck
- You get things done without formal authority, by earning trust across sales, product and engineering
- You’re comfortable moving between the big picture and the detail in the same day

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Ops
description:
About Cantina: 

Cantina Labs is a social AI company, developing a suite of advanced real-time models that push the boundaries of expression, personality, and realism. We bring characters to life, transforming how people tell stories, connect, and create. We build and power ecosystems. Cantina, our flagship social AI platform, is just the beginning.

If you're excited about the potential AI has to shape human creativity and social interactions, join us in building the future!

About the Role: 

We are looking for an ML Engineer to own the production inference stack for our text-to-speech (TTS) and speech recognition (ASR) models, end to end. Our research team delivers trained model checkpoints; you will productionize them as low-latency, real-time streaming services that run cost-efficiently on GPUs. The role covers the inference engines, the Kubernetes infrastructure they run on, and the performance benchmarking and accuracy validation that let us ship changes safely. You will bridge research and production, and own latency, throughput, cost and accuracy as we scale.

What You’ll Do: 

- 
Build and optimize streaming inference engines for TTS and ASR models, including multi-stage model pipelines.

- 
Optimize latency (time to first chunk, p50/p99) and throughput using continuous batching, CUDA Graphs, torch.compile and mixed precision.

- 
Maintain numerical parity with the reference implementation through automated accuracy regression tests, per stage and end to end.

- 
Deploy and operate GPU inference services on Kubernetes: autoscaling, containerization and infrastructure as code.

- 
Build CI/CD for model artifacts, with model versioning and reproducible releases.

- 
Own observability and performance benchmarking: p50/p99 latency, real-time factor (RTF), GPU utilization and cost per request.

- 
Partner with research to productionize new models.

What You’ll Bring: 

- 
Hands-on experience deploying, scaling and optimizing ML models in production, beyond consuming model APIs.

- 
Working knowledge of the full inference stack, from CUDA kernels to serving frameworks, with depth in some layers; expertise across all of them is not expected.

- 
GPU performance optimization: profiling (Nsight Systems, PyTorch Profiler), memory bandwidth, CPU-GPU synchronization.

- 
Solid understanding of model serving: continuous batching, KV cache management, request scheduling.

- 
Production experience with Kubernetes, CI/CD and cloud infrastructure.

- 
Strong Python and PyTorch, and a rigorous approach to performance benchmarking.

- 
Experience with speech or audio models (TTS, ASR, voice conversion).

- 
Experience with inference frameworks such as vLLM (vLLM-Omni), SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT or Triton Inference Server.

Compensation: 

When determining compensation, a number of factors will be considered, including skills, experience, job scope, location, and competitive compensation market data.

- 
Competitive salary and generous company equity

- 
Medical, dental, and vision insurance – 99.99% of premiums covered by Cantina

- 
42 days of paid time off, including:

- 
15 PTO days

10 sick days

- 
15 company holidays

2 floating holidays

Generous parental leave & fertility support

- 
401(k) retirement savings plan

- 
Lifestyle spending account – $500/month to use however you’d like

- 
Complimentary lunch and snacks for in-office employees

- 
One Medical membership, and more!

This is a build-fast, talk-to-humans, own-the-problem role - not a research role and not a pure-infrastructure role. You'll define what "internal AI" looks like here from scratch.

Who this is for 

You're energized by ambiguity and ownership. You'd rather ship a rough tool this week, watch someone use it, and improve it than spend a month on a perfect spec. You like sitting with a non-technical teammate, understanding their actual workflow, and turning it into something that saves them hours. You're comfortable being the only person who owns a problem end to end.

Who you will work with 

- You'll partner closely with the CEO and founders on identifying the highest-leverage operational problems to solve and shaping where internal AI goes next. This is a rare amount of executive access to an engineering role. 

- You’ll work alongside functional leaders across the business to understand their priorities, surface opportunities , and align on what to build. Your work will be visible and leadership level from day one. 

- Operations, Customer Success, Finance, People/Talent Acquisition, Engineering, IT and Data teams, these are your internal customers and collaborators. You'll embed with them, and learn their workflows and ship tools they actually use. 

What you'll actually build

- An agent that drafts customer success replies from our knowledge base and ticket history

- A Slack-based workflow that routes and pre-fills finance approvals

- An internal eval harness so we can trust the LLM features we ship

- A tool that lets the ops team query [internal system] in plain language

What we're looking for 

- 1–3 years building software — backend services, internal tools, automations, or API-driven apps. Internships and co-ops count.

- Strong in TypeScript and/or Python .

- You've built something with LLMs — an agent, a RAG pipeline, a copilot, a prompt-driven tool — through work, a side project, or coursework. We care that you've shipped, not where.

- Comfortable wiring systems together: APIs, webhooks, SaaS integrations, async workflows.

- You move fast under ambiguity and iterate from real feedback.

Bonus, not required

- Used an orchestration framework (LangChain, Temporal, or similar)

- Worked with vector databases or retrieval systems

- Integrated with Salesforce, Slack, Zendesk, Notion, or Jira

What success looks like 

- First few weeks: shipped your first internal tool and it's in active daily use by a business team.

- Within 2 months: 2–3 tools live, and stakeholders are coming to you with ideas.

- By month 3: you've set the team's baseline practices for evals, prompt management, and safe LLM deployment — the foundation the function grows on.
